docs.title: Welcome to V2X E2E simulator
docs.text:
This project is a simulation system based on the AWSIM project, available on GitHub. It has been enhanced with a range of sensor types and a more realistic environment. One of the key study cases in this project is the simulation of autonomous buses, which incorporates a significant number of cameras to address blind spots during autonomous driving. Examples of applications for this simulation environment include analyzing the positioning of roadside unit sensors and bus sensors to enhance the vision of autonomous buses, as well as evaluating traffic metrics such as congestion due to the presence of autonomous buses within the city.

Our Git repository is currently available Download the Unity package and maps

docs.title: About
docs.text:
This project is part of Cool4 (Cooperative Level 4 Automated Mobility Service), which corresponds to Theme 4 of the Road to the L4 initiative.

The Road to the L4 program is a Research, Development, Demonstration, and Deployment (RDD&D) project funded by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) of Japan. Its goal is to promote the practical realization of Level 4 autonomous driving through collaboration among government, industry, and academia.

Cool4 (Cooperative Level 4 Automated Mobility Service) focuses on the development and demonstration of cooperative autonomous driving technologies — enabling vehicles, infrastructures, and systems to share information via V2X communication for safe and efficient automated mobility services.

This repository hosts the V2X End-to-End Simulator, designed to evaluate cooperative Level 4 autonomous driving scenarios in Kashiwa-no-ha and other test sites. The simulator supports comprehensive testing and analysis of communication, perception, and decision-making modules in connected automated environments.

docs.title: Extra Features
docs.text:
• Cyclists support
  • Pseudo sensors (computationally lightweight sensors)
  • New types of ROS messages
  • Complete setup for an Autonomous Bus compatible with Autoware
  • Enhanced logging system compatible with OpenStreetMap
  • Tools and techniques to improve the accuracy of 3D models by loading PCD files
  • Multi-Sensor Step Scanning component that generates synchronized data from camera and LiDAR and creates corresponding ground truth positions
  • Pedestrian and cyclist movement patterns compatible with traffic lights and a collision avoidance system to prevent collisions with pedestrians and vehicles
  • Integration of the UnitySensors package with HDRP support (not available in the original library)
  • Teleport feature on the Unity side for the ego vehicle
  • Traffic API updates to remove vehicles in specific scenarios and handle teleport situations
  • Automatic repetition of multiple configurations to test various camera and lidar setups (documentation for this feature is currently incomplete)

docs.title: Camera View Tab
docs.text:
The View panel lets you switch the main scene camera between several viewpoints at run time, directly from the on‑screen UI (inside the right‑side settings canvas).

There are three built‑in views:

# View Description 1 Follow The default chase camera that follows the ego vehicle (the existing FollowCamera). 2 Top View A fixed bird's‑eye camera looking down on the intersection (Camera Top View Int#1). 3 Free Camera A movable fly‑camera you can drive anywhere in the scene.

Only one view is active at a time. When a view is selected, its Camera, AudioListener and optional control script are enabled and every other view's are disabled, so there is always exactly one rendering camera and one audio listener.

docs.title: Using the panel
docs.text:
• Click a button in the View panel, or press the number keys 1 / 2 / 3 to switch views.
  • Press V to show/hide the panel.

docs.title: Free Camera controls
docs.text:
When the Free Camera view is active you can move it freely:

Input Action Right‑mouse drag Look around (pitch / yaw) W / A / S / D Move forward / left / back / right Q / E Move down / up Left Shift (hold) Move faster (sprint) Scroll wheel Dolly forward / back

The Free Camera spawns at the Follow camera's current position and uses unscaled time, so it keeps responding even when the simulation is paused or slowed.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
The feature is driven by two scripts under Assets/V2X/Script/UI/:

  • CameraViewManager — holds the list of views, switches the active camera, highlights the active button and toggles the panel. SelectView(int) is the method wired to each button's OnClick. If Auto Create Movable Camera is enabled, the Free Camera is created automatically at play time (copying the Follow camera's render settings).
  • FreeFlyCamera — the fly‑camera controller used by the Free Camera view. Movement/look speeds are exposed as MoveSpeed, SprintMultiplier, ScrollSpeed and LookSensitivity.

docs.title: Adding another view
docs.text:
1. Add the camera to the Views list on the CameraViewManager component (set its Label, Camera, and optionally a ControlBehaviour to enable only while active).
  2. Add a button to the View panel and wire its OnClick to CameraViewManager.SelectView with the new view's index.
  3. Add the button to the manager's UI Buttons list (same order as Views) so it highlights when active.

docs.title: Logs System
docs.text: The simulator has two complementary logging components. LogArea monitors all NPCs that pass through a defined trigger zone and writes their state to CSV files. LogAutonomous tracks the ego vehicle's own motion and collision events, and also records spawn selection data written by the Teleporter.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
LogArea is a BoxCollider trigger that maintains live lists of vehicles and pedestrians currently inside it. Every few frames (or every few seconds), it writes a row per tracked NPC to separate CSV files for humans and cars.

The green box in the scene view marks the LogArea trigger volume.

Sample CSV output from LogArea.

docs.title: Logging Modes
docs.text:
LogArea supports two timing modes, controlled by the ultraMode toggle:

Mode Toggle Field Description Frame-based ultraMode = true (default) waitForFrame Log every N frames (default: 2). High-frequency output, best for smooth data. Time-based ultraMode = false waitTime Log every N seconds (default: 0.05 s). Useful when frame rate varies.

Logging starts after a short random delay (20–30 frames). Each sample writes one row per tracked object.

docs.title: Detection Logic
docs.text:
LogArea uses OnTriggerEnter / OnTriggerExit to add and remove objects from its tracking lists:

Object Detected by Tracked as Requires NPC vehicle NPCVehicle component (in the collider's parents) car checkCars Pedestrian NPCPedestrian or WaypointFollower component (in the collider's parents) human checkHumans Other vehicle (e.g. the ego bus) Collider on a layer in vehicleLayer, with a Rigidbody in its hierarchy car checkCars

Destroyed objects are removed from the lists automatically at the next sample.

docs.title: Sensor Column
docs.text:
The Sensor Names column contains the sensors that can currently observe the object, as reported by its LineOfSight component. Each entry has the form name*points* (sensor name and number of detected points), and entries are joined by |. The column is empty for objects without a LineOfSight component.

Color coding used in the companion heat-map tool:

  • Green — NPC seen by the autonomous car
  • Red — NPC not seen
  • Blue — NPC detected by a roadside sensor

Typical placement of LogArea components in the scene.

docs.title: Inspector Fields
docs.text: Field Default Description logPathHumans — Base path of the human CSV (a timestamped file is created per run, see Output Files) logPathCars — Base path of the vehicle CSV (timestamped per run) checkHumans true Track pedestrians (NPCPedestrian / WaypointFollower) and create the human file checkCars true Track NPCVehicles and vehicle-layer bodies and create the car file waitTime 0.05 s Log interval (time-based mode) waitForFrame 2 Log interval in frames (frame-based mode) ultraMode true Use frame-based timing checkpointJumper — CheckpointJumper (implements ILogIndex) whose current index is written to the Index column vehicleLayer — Layer mask for detecting vehicles that are not NPCVehicles (e.g. the bus)

docs.title: CSV Column Reference — Cars and Humans
docs.text:
Both files have the same 20 columns; only the first header differs (Car ID in the car file, Human ID in the human file).

# Column Description 1 Car ID / Human ID NPCVehicle.VehicleID for NPC vehicles; ScenarioHumanId for pedestrians (assigned on first log if missing). Empty for rows without either (e.g. the ego bus) 2 Name GameObject name 3–5 X, Y, Z Position in ROS coordinates plus the MGRS offset (m) 6–9 W rotation, X rotation, Y rotation, Z rotation Orientation as a ROS quaternion 10–11 Time_sec, Time_nano ROS simulation time (seconds, nanoseconds) 12 SystemTimeMs Host wall-clock time, UTC Unix milliseconds 13 Frame Unity frame count 14 Box_State LineOfSight box state; Unknown if the object has no LineOfSight 15 Sensor Names name*points* entries joined by | (see above) 16 Index Current index of checkpointJumper (ILogIndex); 0 if unset 17–19 X Speed, Y Speed, Z Speed transform.forward × speed (Unity world axes, not ROS) 20 Speed Amount Scalar speed from the object's ISpeed component (m/s); 0 if it has none

Note

Numbers are always written with . as decimal separator, regardless of the system locale.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
LogAutonomous is attached directly to the ego vehicle. It continuously logs the vehicle's position, velocity, and acceleration, and records collision events. It also receives spawn selection data from the Teleporter after each teleport.

LogAutonomous component in the Inspector.

Sample CSV output from LogAutonomous.

docs.title: Ego Vehicle State Log
docs.text:
Every waitTime seconds (default 0.005 s, i.e. effectively every frame) LogAutonomous appends one row:

# Column Description 1–3 X, Y, Z Ego position in ROS coordinates plus the MGRS offset (m) 4–7 W rotation, X rotation, Y rotation, Z rotation Ego orientation as a ROS quaternion 8–10 X velocity, Y velocity, Z velocity Rigidbody linear velocity in the ROS frame (m/s); 0 if there is no Rigidbody 11–13 X acceleration, Y acceleration, Z acceleration Change of velocity since the previous row divided by the elapsed time, ROS frame (m/s²); 0 on the first row 14 list of car collisions Names of bodies in physical contact (OnCollisionEnter), joined by | 15 list of human collisions Names of bodies inside the ego's trigger colliders (OnTriggerEnter), joined by | 16–17 time, nano ROS simulation time (seconds, nanoseconds) 18 system_time_ms Host wall-clock time, UTC Unix milliseconds

Both collision lists only consider colliders on the Vehicle layer (layer 6) and store the object owning the nearest Rigidbody. Entries are removed on OnCollisionExit / OnTriggerExit (not cleared every frame); an empty list is written as a single space.

Note

Some header names contain surrounding spaces (e.g. X velocity, time). Trim header names when parsing. Numbers are always written with . as decimal separator.

docs.title: Spawn Selection Log
docs.text:
After each teleport, the Teleporter calls LogSpawnSelection() on the vehicle's LogAutonomous, which appends a row to a separate spawn-selection CSV file.

Column Description midpoint_segment Name of the target midpoint lane (None if not set) spawn_lane Lane chosen for the spawn (or RandomPoint) sample_index Index of the sampled point on the spawn lane distance_to_midpoint_m Path distance to the midpoint (m) estimated_time_s Kinematic ETA to midpoint (s) target_time_s Randomly drawn target arrival time (s) reached_cruise 1 if cruise speed is reached before the midpoint, else 0 target_x, target_y, target_z Teleport destination in ROS map coordinates (ROS + MGRS offset, same frame as the ego log) ros_time_sec, ros_time_nsec ROS simulation time of the teleport

This log is the primary tool for verifying that the Teleporter is placing the vehicle at the intended arrival times.

docs.title: Inspector Fields
docs.text: Field Default Description logPathCars — Base path of the ego state CSV spawnSelectionLogPath AutonomousSpawnValidation.csv Base path of the spawn selection CSV logFilePrefix Auto Prefix added to both file names (empty = no prefix) waitTime 0.005 s Interval between ego state rows

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
Each run creates new timestamped files; nothing is appended to files from earlier runs. The timestamp is the local start time of the component.

Component Field Resulting file LogArea logPathHumans, logPathCars <dir>/<basename>_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss<ext> LogAutonomous logPathCars <dir>/<logFilePrefix>_<basename>_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss<ext> LogAutonomous spawnSelectionLogPath <dir>/<logFilePrefix>_<basename>_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss<ext>
  • <ext> defaults to .csv if the base path has no extension. An empty base path disables that file.
  • The output directory is created automatically.
  • Relative paths are resolved against the process working directory: the project root in the Editor, the launch directory for a player build.
  • LogAutonomous logs a warning on write errors and keeps logging.

Note

SimulationOutput/ is not git-ignored. Keep log output out of commits manually (or write it outside the repository).

docs.title: Changes / Migration
docs.text:
Analysis scripts written for older versions need updating:

  • LogArea columns shifted: a leading Car ID / Human ID column and a SystemTimeMs column (after Time_nano) were added. Select columns by header name rather than position.
  • One file per run: LogArea and LogAutonomous no longer append to a fixed path; each run writes new _yyyyMMdd_HHmmss files (LogAutonomous files also get the logFilePrefix). Read the newest file or glob all runs.
  • LogAutonomous acceleration is now the real acceleration (m/s²); previously the acceleration columns duplicated the velocity.
  • NPCPedestrian humans are now logged by LogArea (previously only WaypointFollower humans).
  • LogAutonomous gained a trailing system_time_ms column and the spawn-selection log.
  • Numbers are written locale-independently (. decimal separator).

docs.title: MultiSensor Step Scanning (LiDAR + Camera)
docs.text:
Namespace: AWSIM.Scanning Script: MultiSensorStepScanning.cs

A unified, step-based scanning system for LiDAR and camera sensors in Unity. Designed for AWSIM / RGLUnityPlugin, this tool enables synchronized LiDAR and camera captures on a per-step basis, useful for dataset generation, ground-truth logging, or robotic simulation. The most important aspect of this component is ensuring that all elements are captured simultaneously, preventing any blurring or misalignment in the camera image.

docs.title: 🧭 Overview
docs.text: MultiSensorStepScanning coordinates LiDAR and camera captures frame-by-frame, ensuring precise, motion-free outputs. Each “step” freezes the Unity simulation (Time.timeScale = 0), triggers all sensors, and saves outputs before resuming time. The script also supports ground truth logging of detected objects via configured GroundTruthArea components.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• LiDAR Scanning
  • Builds RGL subgraphs per LiDAR sensor.
  • Supports local ROS axes or global ROS world transformations.
  • Optional voxel downsampling for .pcd output files.

  • Saves results under Assets/{outputDirectoryRoot}/Lidar.

  • Camera Scanning

  • Captures one image per configured camera each step.
  • Supports existing custom capture components or built-in fallback capture.
  • Configurable resolution, supersampling, and image format (.png / .jpg).

  • Saves images under Assets/{outputDirectoryRoot}/Camera.

  • Ground Truth CSV Logging

  • Aggregates visible objects from assigned GroundTruthArea volumes.
  • Logs object name, UUID, ROS-space position, yaw, and step index.

  • CSV outputs saved under Assets/{outputDirectoryRoot}/GroundTruthPos.

  • Triggering

  • Manually via Space key.
  • Or programmatically via TriggerAndSaveStep() / coroutine variant.

docs.title: 1. Add the Script
docs.text: Attach MultiSensorStepScanning to an empty GameObject in your Unity scene.

docs.title: 2. Configure Sensors
docs.text: In the Inspector panel:

docs.title: LiDAR
docs.text:
• Assign all GameObjects containing LidarSensor components.
  • Choose coordinate frame mode:
  • Local (default, ROS axes)
  • Global (transforms using worldOriginROS)
  • Enable/disable downsampling and adjust leaf size.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
• Assign all GameObjects with Camera components.
  • Optionally define:
  • Override resolution and supersampling.
  • Image format (PNG/JPG) and quality.
  • Custom capture component name (e.g., "MyCustomCameraFeature").

docs.title: Ground Truth (optional)
docs.text:
• Add one or more GroundTruthArea volumes.
  • Optionally specify a rosReference transform to define relative frame.
  • Enable CSV header writing if desired.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Choose root folder name under Assets/.
  • Enable or disable per-sensor subfolders.
  • The step index will auto-increment after each capture.

docs.title: ⌨️ Triggering a Step
docs.text:
Manual: Press Space in Play Mode.

Programmatic: 

var scanner = FindObjectOfType<MultiSensorStepScanning>();
scanner.TriggerAndSaveStep();

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Vehicle Despawn System removes NPC vehicles within a specified radius. It is used before moving the ego vehicle (Bus or Lexus) to a new position, to prevent collisions with NPCs at the destination. In-code callers are the Teleporter gate and ScenarioSelector (Q/E/F/X start points); TestTrafficRemovingNpc is a manual test component.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The system uses a two-phase approach:

  1. Mark Phase: Vehicles within radius are flagged for removal
  2. Despawn Phase: Flagged vehicles are destroyed in the next FixedUpdate()

docs.title: System Flow
docs.text:
Game Code (Teleporter, ScenarioSelector, TestTrafficRemovingNpc)
    ↓
TrafficManager.RemoveVehiclesInRadius()
    ↓
NPCVehicleSimulator.RemoveVehiclesInRadius()
    ↓
NPCVehicleInternalState (ShouldDespawn = true)
    ↓
TrafficManager.FixedUpdate() → Despawn()

docs.title: Basic Implementation
docs.text:
using AWSIM.TrafficSimulation;
using UnityEngine;

public class TestTrafficRemovingNpc : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] TrafficManager trafficManager;
    [SerializeField] Transform centerTransform;
    [SerializeField] float radius;
    [SerializeField] KeyCode RemoveKey = KeyCode.R;

    private void FixedUpdate()
    {
        if (Input.GetKeyDown(RemoveKey))
        {
            trafficManager.RemoveVehiclesInRadius(centerTransform, radius);
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Component Setup
docs.text: Inspector Parameters: - Traffic Manager: Reference to the TrafficManager in the scene - Center Transform: The center point for vehicle removal (e.g. the ego vehicle transform) - Radius: Distance in meters from center point - Remove Key: Keyboard key to trigger removal (default: R)

docs.title: RemoveVehiclesInRadius
docs.text:
Overloads: - TrafficManager.RemoveVehiclesInRadius(Vector3 center, float radius) - TrafficManager.RemoveVehiclesInRadius(Transform centerTransform, float radius) - uses centerTransform.position; logs a warning and returns 0 if the transform is null

Parameters: - center / centerTransform - Center point of removal area - radius (float) - Radius in meters

Returns: int - Number of vehicles marked for removal (vehicles already marked are not counted again). Returns 0 with a warning if the NPCVehicleSimulator is not initialized.

The call affects only the NPCs of the TrafficManager it is called on. If the scene has several TrafficManagers, call it on each (the Teleporter and ScenarioSelector do this).

docs.title: Distance Calculation
docs.text:
The system uses squared distance (sqrMagnitude) for performance: 

var distanceSquared = (state.Position - centerPosition).sqrMagnitude;
if (distanceSquared <= radiusSquared)
{
    vehicleState.ShouldDespawn = true;
}

docs.title: Despawn Timing
docs.text: Vehicles are not destroyed immediately. Destruction occurs at the end of the next TrafficManager.FixedUpdate() (typically ~0.02 seconds later).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
1. Add TestTrafficRemovingNpc component to any GameObject
  2. Assign the TrafficManager reference from the scene
  3. Set the center transform (ego vehicle or target location)
  4. Configure the radius (recommended: 20-30m)
  5. Enter Play mode and press R key to test removal

docs.title: Performance Notes
docs.text:
• Time Complexity: O(n) where n is the number of active vehicles
  • Optimization: Uses squared distance to avoid expensive square root calculations
  • Recommended Radius: 20-30m when clearing an area around a spawn point

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Vehicles still visible after pressing the key - Wait one FixedUpdate() cycle. Destruction is deferred, not immediate.

Nothing happens when pressing the key - Verify TrafficManager reference is assigned in Inspector - Check that vehicles exist within the specified radius - Ensure the key code matches your input

Performance drops when removing vehicles - Reduce the radius value - Avoid calling the function every frame

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The test component uses FixedUpdate() with Input.GetKeyDown() for testing purposes
  • In production, call RemoveVehiclesInRadius() before teleporting or spawning the ego vehicle
  • Vehicles marked for despawn remain in the scene until next physics update

Related: Traffic Spawning System, Teleporter

docs.title: Lidar PCD Extractor Component
docs.text:
This component captures separate point clouds for static and dynamic points:

  • Static points are candidates for RSU (Roadside Unit) placement.
  • Dynamic points represent positions on the car where LiDAR sensors would be used for an autonomous vehicle.

Captured files are named according to the time step and saved accordingly. Compared to the default PCD component of AWSIM, which only supports a dynamic scanner with a single sensor and merges all files. The path of the autonomous vehicle can be provided in two ways:

  1. CSV File: A CSV file containing scan positions is provided.

  2. Lanelet Map: A lanelet map is given, and the scans are generated along the path.

Sample scan captured by a static sensor

docs.title: Prefab
docs.text: To facilitate easier usage of this component, we have created a prefab located at:

docs.title: Lidar types
docs.text:
As shown in the image above, two types of sensors can be defined: dynamic and static lidar scanners.

  • Dynamic Sensors: These sensors move with the car.
  • Static Sensors: These sensors function as roadside unit sensors that remain stationary during the simulation.

Ensure that all of these sensors, in addition to having the Lidar Sensor component (which all lidar sensors have in AWSIM), also have the RGLScanAdapter component. The code automatically finds these sensors and captures a shot from each position with the defined features on each of them.

docs.title: Vehicle object
docs.text: The BusAutoware object does not perform any functionality in this context and does not run according to the logic of an autonomous vehicle. Therefore, we have disabled all internal functionalities of this component. The purpose of this component is solely to provide realistic observations for dynamic sensors and to correctly represent blind spot positions. In other words, it acts merely as an obstruction of view, which is its intended role.

docs.title: Lidar PCD Extractor
docs.text:
This component is mainly responsible for methods to capture data. The first method uses lanelets: when using the lanelet option, the scanner moves along the lines of the lanelet and scans the positions. The difference of this package compared to the original one is that the shots are stored separately and don't accumulate together.

The second method is using 'Read Poses From File'. When this option is set to true, you can use a CSV file as positions of the car. Then the system only captures the specific points that you have already inserted in the file. The file inputs positions and rotations.

docs.title: Iteration
docs.text: Iteration is the number of times that the test scenario is repeated. This feature helps to capture different types and conditions of cars, and also helps to collect complete data. The vehicle object has the 'Scanner Car' component, which is responsible for evaluating whether the state of the bus is reasonable or not. In case of collision of the bus with another object, or if the sensors intersect with another car, this capture will be denied (these cases occur because during these scan scenarios we only set the position of the car as specified in the file, and it may not be compatible with the current state which is actually available in the city).

docs.title: Wait After Each Scan
docs.text: We recommend setting it to 0, but if you want to see the process work at a slower speed, set a number that you prefer.

docs.title: Sensor Search
docs.text:
There is no need to assign it, but if you assign the Sensor Search component to the same object, it will use it and automatically find and fill it.

The Sensor Search component is optional. This component will explore different setups of angles and positions and will create different states that could compare the results of each position in the final scans, which are separately captured.

docs.title: Vehicle Game Object
docs.text: This is a reference to the vehicle object. Consider that this game object is just a symbol and does not need to have movement logic; the lidar extractor component will move it in the city.

docs.title: Output Files Direction
docs.text:
• Output PCD File Path: The files of the lidar scan will be saved in the directory with the prefix that you have set at the end of this string.
  • Output CSV File Path: In this directory, with this name, a CSV file will be created that shows the position, rotation, and extra information of sensors. This file is required to understand which PCD file is related to which experiment and which sensor.

docs.title: Root Static Sensors
docs.text: This is a reference to an object that is the parent of the static sensors. In the code, we will search the children of this object to find the static sensors.

docs.title: Wait Time
docs.text: This is the time that the entire system lets the city run its traffic before sampling starts.

docs.title: Log Around the Car
docs.text:
'Log Around the Car' is a component that is attached to the vehicle and saves the logs of cars which are near the car in the scan environment. You can leave it null or entirely ignore it, but it will save some data related to blind spots and cars or vehicles that are never seen or seen by which sensors.

Lidar PCD Extractor and Sensor Search

docs.title: PCD Scanner Package (old)
docs.text:
Scanner Package

Note : The current separate package associated with this component is not updated, but it works well. Some parts of the description have been updated with new features. Therefore, use this documentation only if you are working with the old scanner package and not the latest complete package.

This package is developed based on the \"PointCloudMapping\" system of Awsim, which is used to create a point cloud of a city. Our package aims to capture and save the point cloud of the city separately, point by point, but in a more realistic environment. This package can be used alongside the traffic system of the city to simulate input data when different traffic conditions are applied to the city.

You may encounter an error when importing our package.

To resolve this, simply change the following line of code:

Same for second error

How to use

First, duplicate your base scene, which has a 3D map and can include the traffic system. In my case, I duplicated PointCloudMapping and renamed it to PointCloudScanner.

Now, go to Assets/ScannerPackage/Prefab and drag and drop the prefab into the scene.

Because we already have the RGL component in our prefab, we must remove the RGL Scene Manage component from the scene. In your case, if you are building your scene from scratch, you may not be required to do the same.

In the PointCloudScanner, there are two components: Point CloudMapper, which performs the normal scanning, and Lidar Pcd Extractor, which scans the environment frame by frame.

Configuring the Components:

This package supports multiple static and dynamic sensors. Dynamic sensors are the sensors carried by the car, while static sensors remain in the same place all the time during scanning.

For example, in the image below, you can see we have three dynamic lidars on our car. Since the position of sensors is relative to the parent, it is possible to choose the position of each sensor independently. The log system will save the position of each sensor in each frame. However, you must ensure that sensor names are unique, as the log file saves data by the name of the sensor, and unique names are necessary for identification in the log file.

Similarly, we have two static lidars. Our code only checks the children of the "Statics" component. In this section, you can duplicate or add different sensors as needed.

** As you can see in the lidar object, the lidar objects in this prefab must have an RGL scan adapter. We recommend using our sensors and duplicating them to create new sensors to avoid missing this component. However, if you want to create it from scratch, you can manually add this component at the end of your components in the lidar or each sensor that you use.

The traffic system does not need to be inside our object and only needs to run simultaneously.

For Developers: The logic of the code uses a box collider of the scanner car to detect whether it is inside a car or not. If it is outside the car, it will scan in that step. If not, it won't scan and will skip that step.

Lidar PCD Extractor(in Point cloud scanner object)

Check the Path of PCD and CSV: The path is relative to the Asset file.

Osm Container: This is the lanelet through which the scanner travels.

Wait Time: This is the amount of time the system waits for the traffic system or other systems to start working. After this period, the process of capturing will begin.

World Origin ROS: It is very important to configure this based on the real position of your map location. The default position of the package is set for Kashiwa, and you must edit this field according to your project.

Lanelet Visualizer is Active: Controls the visibility of the path lines that cars travel through.

Use CarPos: Hold off on using this feature as it does not work yet.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Pedestrian and cyclist paths can be defined in a JSON file instead of being placed by hand in the scene. At start-up the file is read, one runtime WaypointSystem is built per path, and pooled agents with a WaypointFollower are spawned onto each path at the configured rate.

pedestrian_spawn.json ──► WaypointSystem per path ──► pooled WaypointFollower agents
 (ROS/MGRS coordinates)    (Unity coordinates,          (spawned at spawnPerMinute,
                            optional light constraints)  recycled at path end)
Component Status Role PedestrianCyclistSpawner Supported — active in the NormalTraffics scenario of the Kashiwa scene (GameObject ScenarioSelector/Cool4 Kakeiken Overal Evaluation/PedestrianCyclistSpawner) Loads the JSON, builds the paths and spawns both pedestrians and cyclists PathConfigLoader + PedestrianPathSpawner / CyclistPathSpawner Alternative — present in the scene but inactive Loader builds the paths; two separate spawners use them ClearWaypointFollower Alternative follower Rigidbody follower that can read a path from PathConfigLoader PathMetadata Helper Stores type and spawnPerMinute on each generated path GameObject

All scripts are in Assets/V2X/Script/Paths/ (namespace V2X.Paths).

docs.title: The JSON File
docs.text: Default path: Assets/Configs/pedestrian_spawn.json

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
{
  "paths": [
    {
      "id": "<unique string>",
      "type": "pedestrian | cyclist | both",
      "spawnPerMinute": 0.0,
      "waypoints": [
        { "x": 0.0, "y": 0.0, "z": 0.0, "checkLight": false, "trafficLightId": "" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Path
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Required and unique. Paths with an empty id are skipped. If two paths share an id, both entries spawn on the waypoints of the last one. type string pedestrian, cyclist or both (case-insensitive). Empty or unknown values are treated as both. Selects which prefabs may be spawned on the path. spawnPerMinute float Mean spawn rate for this path. 0 (or negative) disables the path. waypoints array Ordered points. Paths with no waypoints are skipped.

docs.title: Waypoint
docs.text:
Field Type Description x, y, z float Position in metres in the ROS / MGRS map frame (the same frame as the Lanelet2 / point-cloud map). checkLight bool If true (and trafficLightId is set), a ConstraintPedestrianTrafficLight is added at this waypoint. trafficLightId string GameObject name of the pedestrian TrafficLight to check (matched case-insensitively). The agent waits at this waypoint until the light is solid green.

Traffic light names must be unique

The light is looked up by name among all TrafficLight components in the scene (including inactive ones) and the first match is used. If several lights share the name, the agent may watch the wrong one. For example, the current Kashiwa scene contains three TrafficLight objects named TrafficLights_B_pedestrain (2), which is referenced by the bundled configs. Rename lights so that every referenced name is unique. If the light is not found, a warning is logged and the agent does not stop there.

Context Assets/Configs/pedestrian_spawn.json resolves to Unity Editor <project>/Assets/Configs/pedestrian_spawn.json Player build <build folder>/Assets/Configs/pedestrian_spawn.json (the folder that contains the executable and its _Data folder)

Player builds

docs.text:
File Total rate pedestrian_spawn.json (default; same content as the Low preset) ≈ 47 agents per hour pedestrian_spawn-KashiwaRealPedestrains_Low_total47.json ≈ 47 agents per hour (sum of spawnPerMinute = 0.779) pedestrian_spawn-KashiwaRealPedestrains_High_total76.json ≈ 76 agents per hour (sum of spawnPerMinute = 1.273)

All presets define the same 14 Kashiwa paths (Path1–Path14, type both) and differ only in spawnPerMinute. To use a preset, set pathsJsonPath on PedestrianCyclistSpawner to its path (or copy it over pedestrian_spawn.json).

docs.title: Coordinate Conversion
docs.text:
Each JSON point is converted to a Unity world position as follows:

  1. Subtract the MGRS offset (only if useMgrsOffset is on): the offset is Environment.Instance.MgrsOffsetPosition. If there is no Environment in the scene, manualOffset is used instead (a ROS/MGRS-frame offset; ignored when it is zero).
  2. ROS → Unity axes: (x, y, z) → (-y, z, x).
  3. Add worldOrigin: if a worldOrigin Transform is assigned, its position is added (a Unity-frame translation).
  4. Ground snapping (if snapWaypointsToGround is on): a ray is cast downward from groundRayHeight metres above the point, over a distance of 2 × groundRayHeight, against groundMask. On a hit, the height is replaced by the hit point. On a miss, the converted height is kept.

Saving applies the inverse conversion (Unity → ROS: (x, y, z) → (z, -x, y), then add the offset).

docs.title: Inspector Fields
docs.text:
Field Default Description pedestrianPrefabs — Pedestrian prefabs (must have a WaypointFollower) cyclistPrefabs — Cyclist prefabs (must have a WaypointFollower) activeParent — Optional parent for spawned agents maxExtraInstancesPerSpawn 5 When no compatible inactive clone exists, a new clone is created. 0 forbids creating clones (and since the pool starts empty, nothing spawns) maxActive 0 Max concurrently active agents across all paths of this spawner. 0 = unlimited. The Kashiwa scene uses 5 initialSpawnDelayRange (0, 2) Random delay before a path's first spawn (seconds). The Kashiwa scene uses (0, 0) worldOrigin — Optional Unity-frame anchor added after conversion useMgrsOffset true Subtract the MGRS offset of Environment manualOffset (0, 0, 0) ROS/MGRS-frame offset used when useMgrsOffset is on but no Environment exists snapWaypointsToGround true Snap waypoints to the ground with a downward raycast groundMask Everything Layers hit by the ground ray groundRayHeight 3 Ray start height above the waypoint (m) npcPaths — Paths loaded from the JSON (filled at runtime; editable in the Scene view) pathsJsonPath Assets/Configs/pedestrian_spawn.json JSON file to load / save

The JSON is loaded in Start. The context menu provides Load NPC Paths From JSON (reload and restart all spawn loops) and Save NPC Paths To JSON (overwrite pathsJsonPath with npcPaths).

docs.title: Spawn Timing
docs.text:
For each enabled path, a separate spawn loop runs:

  • Mean interval = 60 / spawnPerMinute seconds (minimum 0.1 s).
  • First spawn: after a random delay from initialSpawnDelayRange. If that delay is 0, a random phase in [0, interval) is used instead, so paths do not spawn in sync.
  • Following spawns: each wait is drawn from a Gaussian around the mean interval (standard deviation 10 %), clamped to 0.5×–1.5× the mean.
  • If maxActive is reached, the loop waits one mean interval and checks again.

docs.title: Pooling and Recycling
docs.text:
• Agents are created as clones of a random prefab from the lists allowed by the path type (pedestrian → pedestrianPrefabs, cyclist → cyclistPrefabs, both → both lists), and kept in a pool.
  • An inactive clone is reused only on a compatible path: a cyclist clone is never reused on a pedestrian path, and a pedestrian clone is never reused on a cyclist path. Any clone can be reused on a both path.
  • On spawn, the agent is placed at the first waypoint (ForceStartAtFirstWaypoint), receives a new ScenarioHumanId, and is activated.
  • Generated paths do not loop. At the last waypoint, WaypointFollower deactivates the agent, which returns it to the pool.

The generated path objects (Path_<id> with wp children, under RuntimePaths_PedCyclist) are hidden from the Hierarchy.

docs.title: Editing Paths in the Scene View
docs.text:
PedestrianCyclistSpawnerEditor (Assets/V2X/Editor/) adds a Path Editing section to the Inspector once npcPaths contains paths:

Control Description Selected Path Path to show in the Scene view Handle Size Size of the waypoint handles Show Labels Show <id>:<index> labels

The selected path is drawn as lines between its waypoints (green = pedestrian, cyan = cyclist, yellow = both) with a sphere handle at each waypoint. Dragging a handle converts its position back to ROS/MGRS and updates npcPaths (with Undo). Use Save NPC Paths To JSON to write the change to the file.

Note

npcPaths is serialized with the scene, so handles are available in Edit mode too, but Start always replaces npcPaths with the JSON content. Save to JSON for an edit to take effect. During Play, moving handles does not move the running waypoint systems; they are rebuilt only when the paths are loaded again.

docs.title: Alternative: PathConfigLoader + Pedestrian/CyclistPathSpawner
docs.text:
In this setup, PathConfigLoader loads the JSON in Awake and builds the waypoint systems. PedestrianPathSpawner and CyclistPathSpawner read them in Start (finding a loader in the scene if none is assigned). In the Kashiwa scene these objects exist under the NormalTraffics scenario but are inactive, and the loader's jsonConfigPath is set to Assets/Configs/paths.json.

Spawner Paths used Prefabs PedestrianPathSpawner pedestrian and both pedestrianPrefabs; on both paths also cyclistPrefabsForBoth (cyclist clones are reused only on both paths) CyclistPathSpawner cyclist only cyclistPrefabs

Both spawners have activeParent, maxExtraInstancesPerSpawn (5 / 3), maxActive (0) and initialSpawnDelayRange (0, 2), with the same timing rules as above (maxActive is counted per spawner).

If empty, a RuntimePaths GameObject is created instantiateEditableInScene false If true, generated Path_<id> objects are normal scene objects that can be moved; otherwise they are hidden (HideAndDontSave) worldOrigin — Optional Unity-frame anchor added after conversion useMgrsOffset true Subtract the MGRS offset of Environment manualOffset (0, 0, 0) ROS/MGRS-frame offset used when no Environment exists snapWaypointsToGround true Snap waypoints to the ground groundMask Everything Layers hit by the ground ray groundRayHeight 3 Ray start height above the waypoint (m)

The Inspector has Load Paths Now and Save Paths Now buttons (also available as the context menu items Load Paths JSON / Save Paths JSON).

Save writes the current positions of the wp children of each Path_<id> object back to the JSON. It also picks up WaypointSystem objects that were duplicated in the scene: the id is the object name without the Path_ prefix. type and spawnPerMinute are read from the object's PathMetadata component. checkLight / trafficLightId are kept only where a ConstraintPedestrianTrafficLight with a resolved light exists on the waypoint.

Warning

If runtimeParent is not set, Save collects every WaypointSystem in the scene, including hand-made ones. Set runtimeParent before saving.

docs.title: PathMetadata
docs.text: PathMetadata (type, spawnPerMinute) is added to every generated Path_<id> object by both PathConfigLoader and PedestrianCyclistSpawner. With instantiateEditableInScene enabled, edit it in the Inspector to change a path's type or rate before saving.

docs.title: ClearWaypointFollower
docs.text: ClearWaypointFollower is an alternative rigidbody follower (acceleration/deceleration, look-ahead steering, optional per-waypoint waits and NoLoop / Loop / PingPong modes). With pathSource = PathLoader and a pathId, it reads the path from PathConfigLoader (found in the scene if not assigned). It uses the loader's converted waypoint positions (the children of the generated WaypointSystem), so the offset and ground snapping match the loader, and takes only checkLight / trafficLightId from the JSON definition. It is not used by the spawners above.

docs.title: Changing the JSON at Runtime
docs.text:
The Traffic settings panel of the UI (TrafficSettingsUI) has a pedestrian path input field. Its Apply button calls SetJsonConfigPath(...) and LoadPaths() on the first PathConfigLoader it finds, including inactive ones.

Warning

This field targets PathConfigLoader only. It does not affect PedestrianCyclistSpawner, which is the spawner used in the Kashiwa scene. Already running PedestrianPathSpawner / CyclistPathSpawner instances also keep the paths they read in Start. To change the pedestrian config of the supported spawner, set pathsJsonPath in the Inspector (or replace the file) before Play.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / Fix No pedestrians or cyclists spawn The JSON was not found (Paths JSON not found at ... warning). In a player build, copy Assets/Configs/ next to the executable. Also check that the NormalTraffics scenario is selected A specific path never spawns spawnPerMinute is 0 or negative, id is empty, or the path has no waypoints Fewer agents than expected maxActive is reached (the Kashiwa scene uses 5), or the prefab list for the path type is empty, or maxExtraInstancesPerSpawn is 0 Agents appear in the wrong place or far away Offset settings: keep useMgrsOffset on when the JSON uses MGRS map coordinates and the scene has an Environment. Without an Environment, set manualOffset. The agent will not stop at that waypoint Agent waits at the wrong light or never crosses The light name is not unique and another light with the same name was matched. Rename the lights so the referenced name is unique

docs.title: Pedestrian
docs.text:
Each pedestrian has three script components, as shown in the picture:

  1. NPC Pedestrian : This component handles and checks the physics behavior of the model. The log system uses this component to determine if an object is a human (this applies to cyclists as well).

  2. Simple PedestrianWalker Controller2 : This component enables NPCs to move and return over crosswalks

    • Duration : Time of movement
    • Speed : Speed of movement
    • Traffic light : If this field is assigned, the character will check the color of the traffic light before moving into the street. If left null, the character skips this check and, after the duration time, will rotate and return to the initial position, looping this back-and-forth movement infinitely.
    • Check Traffic Ligh Time : Frequency of scanning the traffic light state when character wants to cross the road.
    • Wait Time : Duration of the character's waiting time when reaching the end of movement before starting to come back.

  1. Line of sight : Similar to the Vehcile section and psudo sensor section this component responsible to detecting system of our custom messages

    • Points Parent : representitive points of pedestrian to better understand this section please look at the pesudo sensor section
    • Cube : is a reference to the box which is around the character and show the sate of visibility
    • Box State : is only for testing

Note To copy or create a new pedestrian in the city, you can duplicate the current pedestrians and configure them, or use the prefab located at ASSET/KashiwaPackage/Prefabs/LineOfSight

docs.title: Cyclists
docs.text: Cyclists have similar components compared to pedestrians, but there is one key difference: the "Simple Pedestrian Walker Controller 2" component is replaced with "Simple Cyclist Movement".

docs.title: Noise Setting
docs.text:
Noise Setting is a singleton class responsible for creating noise for all the mock sensors. At the start of their operation, each sensor will check and obtain the related noise for itself.

The numbers in the component show the amount of noise that will be added to the target signal, within a range of [-value, value], in a uniform distribution. The distribution of the noise is uniform and additive to the original values.

As seen in the components, multiple types of noise can be defined with different factors. In the image below, a publisher sends four types of three-dimensional vectors with default noise. By default, if the name written in the field does not match any of the existing noises, it will return the first noise in the list. If the list of noises is empty, the system will consider the data as having no noise.

docs.title: Pseudo Sensor
docs.text:
Pseudo sensors are designed to reduce the number of processes compared to real sensors such as lidar. Unlike real sensors that broadcast signals in all directions, pseudo sensors use line of sight. Rays are directly sent toward target objects that already have a line of sight, as illustrated in the picture below.

Each pseudo sensor requires a Mock Sensor Object and a box collider. The box collider is used to calculate ray collisions.

docs.title: Fields:
docs.text:
• Name : This field is used in the log system to identify which sensors have detected objects.

  • Category : This field categorizes sensors using a config file. If you prefer to manually set the position and features of the sensor in the Unity scene, you can ignore this field.

  • Mock Sensor Type : This enum field determines if the sensor simulates a Camera or lidar and sets it in a bus or roadside.

  • HFOV (Horizontal Field of View) : Specifies the horizontal field of view.

  • VFOV (Vertical Field of View) : Specifies the vertical field of view.

  • Sceen Objects : This field is for testing purposes and shows the detected objects during runtime.

  • Max Distnace : Specifies the range of the rays.

docs.title: Other configuration:
docs.text: At the end the pseudo sensor must be add to scenario this enable the system to detect which object detect by which type of sensors

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Each component that must be detected by a pseudo sensor must have the Line of Sight component. Objects with this component periodically check the Scenario component to determine if they have a line of sight to the sensor within their range. The line of sight is calculated using rays in Unity from the representative to the collider of the sensor, shown in the picture by arrows. Based on the number of points that can see the sensor, the box state for the object will be determined. The configuration of the number of required points to see a sensor, to be considered as a watched point, is defined in the Blind Scenario Manager component. In our case, the AutowareSimulator contains this component.

Pedestrian component

Configuration of thresholds

These thresholds indicate how many representative points of an object must see the sensor to be considered as detected.

docs.title: Color states
docs.text: In our simulation, each car, pedestrian, or cyclist has three states. These states show how the autonomous car can observe these objects. The red state demonstrates that the car has no sense of the object. The purple or blue state means that RSUs (roadside units) detect the object, but the autonomous cars cannot see it. The green state indicates that the object is detected by the autonomous sensors.

docs.title: Sample Scene Setup
docs.text: Figure 1. Example of assigned spawn areas and object pool setup.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The RandomSpawnCharacters component is responsible for randomly placing child objects (for example, characters, agents, or NPCs) that exist in an object pool within predefined spawn areas under the component's GameObject.

Each child area under this component defines a region where characters can appear. The script uses the area size of each region to weight the probability of selection — meaning larger areas are more likely to receive more characters.

docs.title: Component Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Collects all child area Transforms under the component
  • Collects all pooled objects (for example, humans) from the assigned ObjectPool
  • Calculates each area's relative area weight based on its local scale
  • Spawns (or repositions) each human within one of the weighted child areas
  • Repeats the sampling at a fixed interval using Unity's FixedUpdate loop

docs.title: Serialized Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description ObjectPool Transform The parent transform containing pooled objects (for example, humans or NPCs). Each child under this pool will be repositioned. eachPosWaitFrame int The number of frames to wait between each reposition cycle (in FixedUpdate). Default is 4 frames.

docs.title: Internal Variables
docs.text: Variable Type Description childAreas Transform[] Stores all the child transforms under the component. These define the spawn areas. humans LineOfSight[] References to all characters inside the object pool. areaWeights float[] Normalized area weights used for random area selection. timer int Frame-based timer for controlling update intervals.

docs.title: 1. Initialization (Awake)
docs.text:
• Retrieves all child areas under this GameObject
  • Retrieves all human agents under the ObjectPool
  • Calculates area weights via CalculateAreaWeights()

docs.title: 2. Area Weight Calculation
docs.text:
• Each child area contributes proportionally to its surface area (scale.x * scale.z)
  • Weights are normalized to ensure they sum to 1
  • Larger areas have a higher chance of selection

docs.title: 3. Random Section Selection
docs.text: • Uses a weighted random algorithm (GetWeightedRandomSection) to pick which area to place each human in

docs.title: 4. Character Placement
docs.text: For each human: - Chooses a random point within the selected area's bounds - Applies the area's local rotation - Translates the position into world space

docs.title: 5. Continuous Update
docs.text: In FixedUpdate, the code checks if the frame count exceeds the wait threshold and re-samples all character positions accordingly.

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text:
1. Attach RandomSpawnCharacters to a GameObject (for example, SpawnManager)
  2. Create child GameObjects under it to define spawn areas. Adjust each child's Transform.localScale to represent area size
  3. Assign an ObjectPool Transform that contains all characters to be placed
  4. Set eachPosWaitFrame if you want to adjust the update frequency

Tip

Ensure all pooled objects have a LineOfSight component (or adjust the script for your component type).

docs.text:
SpawnManager (with RandomSpawnCharacters)
 ├── Area_1 (Transform defines spawn area)
 ├── Area_2 (Transform defines spawn area)
 └── Area_3 (Transform defines spawn area)

ObjectPool

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The system assumes rectangular spawn regions (x * z)
  • Y-axis height is ignored (flat plane assumption)
  • The parent transform is excluded from spawn area calculations
  • You can extend the script to support:
    • Non-rectangular areas
    • Custom randomization patterns
    • Weighted spawn limits per area

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Teleporter component is a trigger-based system that automatically relocates the ego (autonomous) vehicle to a new spawn position whenever it exits through a designated trigger volume. It handles NPC clearance at the destination, optional delays, and logs the spawn selection data for analysis.

No hotkeys

The Teleporter gate is triggered only by the ego vehicle entering its collider; it has no keyboard shortcuts. The Q/E/F/X keys described in the QuickStart belong to a different feature (ScenarioSelector start points).

Key Design Goal

The Teleporter is designed for repeatable, controlled experiments: by targeting a midpoint lane segment with a randomized arrival time, each run places the ego vehicle at a different distance from a point of interest while keeping the scenario statistically comparable.

docs.title: Spawn Strategies
docs.text:
The Teleporter supports two independent strategies, selectable from the Inspector.

LaneMidpoint (default)RandomPoint

Samples candidate spawn positions along a set of configured TrafficLane objects, then picks the candidate whose estimated travel time to a target midpoint lane is closest to a randomly drawn target time.

This strategy guarantees that the ego vehicle is placed at a realistic driving distance from the point of interest — far enough to observe natural traffic behaviour before reaching it.

Picks a random Transform from a hand-placed list of RandomSpawnPoint entries. Only valid entries (non-null entry with an assigned point) are considered. Each entry can optionally override the rotation with a custom Euler angle.

Use this strategy when you need full manual control over spawn positions without any ETA logic.

docs.title: Candidate Generation
docs.text:
The Teleporter walks through all LaneSpawnSource entries and samples each lane at regular intervals defined by spawnSubdivisionSpacing (default 10 m):

Lane waypoints → cumulative distance table → sample every N metres

If includeSegmentEndpoints is enabled, sampling starts at the lane start (0 m) and the lane end (lane length) is always added as a candidate, even when the length is not a multiple of the spacing. If it is disabled, sampling starts at spawnSubdivisionSpacing and the lane end is only included when it falls on a sample. The spacing is clamped to at least 1 m.

For each sample, the component caches:

  • World position (interpolated along the lane waypoints)
  • Forward direction (used to orient the vehicle on spawn)

docs.title: Distance Calculation (Dijkstra)
docs.text:
For each candidate, the Teleporter computes the driving distance to the configured midpointSegment lane. When the candidate is on a different lane than the midpoint, it runs a lightweight Dijkstra search through the lane graph (NextLanes connections):

cost(start_lane) = lane_length - distance_from_start
cost(next_lane)  = cost(current_lane) + next_lane_length
...
stop when midpointSegment is reached

Candidates with no reachable path to the midpoint are excluded, as are candidates on the midpoint lane itself that lie past the target point.

docs.title: ETA Calculation
docs.text:
Travel time is estimated with a two-phase kinematic model (acceleration + cruise):

\[ t = \begin{cases} \sqrt{\dfrac{2d}{a}} & \text{if } d \leq \dfrac{v_c^2}{2a} \\[10pt] \dfrac{v_c}{a} + \dfrac{d - \dfrac{v_c^2}{2a}}{v_c} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Where:

  • \(d\) = distance to midpoint (metres)
  • \(v_c\) = cruise speed (cruiseSpeedKmh converted to m/s)
  • \(a\) = assumed acceleration (assumedAcceleration)

docs.title: Target Time Selection
docs.text:
Each teleport draws a random target arrival time uniformly from targetArrivalWindow:

t_target ~ Uniform(targetArrivalWindow.x, targetArrivalWindow.y)

The candidate with the smallest |ETA - t_target| is selected.

docs.title: Teleport Sequence and NPC Clearance
docs.text:
When a Vehicle enters the trigger, the Teleporter runs one coroutine per vehicle in this order:

  1. Pick the destination with the selected spawn strategy. If no candidate is found (empty laneSpawnSources, missing or unreachable midpointSegment, or no valid random points), it logs the warning Teleporter: No spawn candidate available. Aborting teleport. and does nothing.
  2. Optional random delay drawn from spawnDelayRange (only if spawnDelayRange.y > 0). The ego vehicle keeps driving during this delay.
  3. Clear NPCs: calls RemoveVehiclesInRadius(destination, clearanceRadius) on every TrafficManager found in the scene at Awake. Clearing happens after the random delay, right before the teleport, so NPCs have little time to drive back into the cleared area.
  4. Wait teleportDelay seconds so the marked NPCs are despawned (see NPC Cars).
  5. Move the ego: sets the Rigidbody kinematic and sets the pose over several FixedUpdate steps.
  6. Log the selection via LogAutonomous.LogSpawnSelection() (if the vehicle has that component).
  7. Restore physics: Rigidbody non-kinematic, position/rotation set, linear and angular velocity zeroed. After two more FixedUpdate steps the vehicle can trigger the gate again.
sequenceDiagram
    participant T as Trigger Volume
    participant TP as Teleporter
    participant TM as TrafficManager
    participant EGO as Ego Vehicle

    T->>TP: OnTriggerEnter (ego vehicle)
    TP->>TP: SelectSpawnCandidate() (abort if none)
    TP->>TP: Wait random delay (spawnDelayRange, optional)
    TP->>TM: RemoveVehiclesInRadius(dest, clearanceRadius)
    TP->>TP: Wait teleportDelay
    TP->>EGO: Rigidbody kinematic = true
    TP->>EGO: SetPositionAndRotation(dest) over FixedUpdates
    TP->>TP: LogSpawnSelection()
    TP->>EGO: kinematic = false, zero velocities

Disabling the gate

If the Teleporter is disabled while a teleport is in progress, OnDisable makes the affected vehicles' Rigidbodies non-kinematic again and clears the in-progress set, so new teleports are allowed once it is re-enabled.

docs.title: Teleport Timing
docs.text: Field Default Description clearanceRadius 10 m Radius around destination to clear NPC vehicles teleportDelay 0.5 s Fixed wait after NPC clearance, before teleport spawnDelayRange (0, 0) Random delay before NPC clearance: X = min, Y = max. Set Y > 0 to enable. The ego keeps driving during this delay.

docs.title: Strategy Selection

docs.title: Lane-Based (Midpoint Targeting)

docs.title: Spawn Selection Logging
docs.text:
After every teleport, the Teleporter calls LogSpawnSelection() on the ego vehicle's LogAutonomous component (if present). This writes one row to the spawn selection CSV:

Column Description midpoint_segment Name of the target midpoint lane (None if not assigned) spawn_lane Name of the selected spawn lane (or RandomPoint) sample_index Index of the sample point on the spawn lane (for RandomPoint: index in randomSpawnPoints) distance_to_midpoint_m Dijkstra path distance to midpoint (m) estimated_time_s Kinematic ETA to midpoint (s) target_time_s Randomly drawn target arrival time (s) reached_cruise 1 if cruise speed is reached before the midpoint, else 0 target_x, target_y, target_z Teleport destination in ROS map coordinates (MGRS local), the same frame as the ego log ros_time_sec, ros_time_nsec ROS time of the teleport

For the RandomPoint strategy, distance_to_midpoint_m, estimated_time_s and target_time_s are 0 and reached_cruise is 0.

The file is named <logFilePrefix>_<name>_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss.csv, where <name> comes from spawnSelectionLogPath (default AutonomousSpawnValidation.csv) and logFilePrefix defaults to Auto. The file is created in the directory of spawnSelectionLogPath, which is created automatically if missing.

See Loggers for details on the full CSV output.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the Trigger Volume
docs.text:
1. Create an empty GameObject.
  2. Add a BoxCollider and enable Is Trigger.
  3. Scale it to cover the exit area of your road loop.
  4. Attach the Teleporter script.

docs.title: Step 2 — Configure Lanes (LaneMidpoint strategy)
docs.text:
1. In the Inspector, add entries to Lane Spawn Sources and assign TrafficLane objects that cover the valid spawn zone.
  2. Assign the Midpoint Segment — the lane the ego vehicle should be heading toward on each run.
  3. Adjust cruiseSpeedKmh and assumedAcceleration to match the ego vehicle's expected behaviour.

docs.title: Step 3 — Tune the Arrival Window
docs.text:
Set targetArrivalWindow to the range of arrival times you want to study. For example:

  • (10, 60) s → the selected spawn has an estimated arrival time close to a random value between 10 and 60 s (limited by the available candidates)
  • (0, 0) → vehicle always spawns as close to the midpoint as possible

To see which arrival times your lanes can actually produce, add the TeleporterDebug component to any GameObject and assign the Teleporter (if left empty, it uses the first Teleporter found). When the component is enabled it logs to the Console each source lane's length, the total length, and the range of ETAs from the closest to the farthest spawn sample to the midpoint target. Choose a targetArrivalWindow inside that range. TeleporterDebug is editor-only; it does nothing in player builds.

Figure 1: Final vehicle position after teleport Figure 2: Trigger gate and BoxCollider in the scene

docs.title: Tips and Best Practices
docs.text:
Lane Coverage

Add lanes that span the full approach zone to the midpoint. More candidates give the system more flexibility to match the target arrival time precisely.

Clearance Radius

Set clearanceRadius large enough to prevent the ego vehicle from spawning inside an NPC. A value of 10–15 m is usually sufficient.

Midpoint Must Be Reachable

If no candidate has a connected path (via NextLanes) to the midpointSegment, the teleport is aborted with the warning No spawn candidate available. Aborting teleport. and the ego keeps driving. TeleporterDebug reports Could not compute distance to midpoint in this case.

Re-trigger Prevention

The Teleporter internally tracks which vehicles are currently being teleported (teleportingVehicles HashSet), so a vehicle re-entering the trigger during the delay phase is ignored.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The RandomTrafficSimulator is responsible for continuously spawning NPC vehicles across a configurable set of lanes. It works within the TrafficManager pipeline and supports per-lane spawn rate control, weighted lane-change probabilities, and a maximum-spawn lifetime.

docs.title: Spawnable Lanes
docs.text:
Each RandomTrafficSimulator instance is given a list of SpawnableLaneConfig entries — one per lane it is allowed to use as a spawn point:

public struct SpawnableLaneConfig {
    public TrafficLane lane;
    public float spawnsPerMinute;   // 0 = no rate limit
}

Every FixedUpdate, the simulator picks a random spawn point from this list and hands it to the TrafficManager. If the spawn is not possible (lane occupied, too close to the ego vehicle, rate limit not elapsed, maxVehicleCount reached), it is skipped; on the next frame a new random lane is picked. The chosen prefab is kept until it is actually spawned, so large vehicles are not starved by small ones.

Entries with no lane assigned are ignored. A simulator with no valid spawnable lane is treated as disabled.

Upgrading older scenes

spawnableLanes used to be a plain TrafficLane[]. Scenes saved with that format show empty {lane, spawnsPerMinute} entries after the upgrade and must be relinked in the Inspector.

docs.title: Maximum Spawns
docs.text:
Setting maximumSpawns > 0 gives the simulator a finite lifetime: it deactivates itself after spawning that many vehicles. This is useful for scripted scenarios where you want exactly N cars on a route.

maximumSpawns = 0  →  unlimited (run forever)
maximumSpawns = N  →  deactivate after N spawns

docs.title: Priority System
docs.text:
When two or more simulators request the same spawn lane at the same time, TrafficManager resolves the conflict using a fair round-robin priority counter:

sequenceDiagram
    participant S1 as Simulator A (priority 0)
    participant S2 as Simulator B (priority 2)
    participant TM as TrafficManager

    S1->>TM: Want to spawn on Lane_X
    S2->>TM: Want to spawn on Lane_X
    TM->>TM: Sort by priority (descending)
    TM->>S2: Attempt spawn → success
    TM->>S1: IncreasePriority(+1)
    TM->>S2: ResetPriority(0)

Each time a simulator loses the race it gains +1 priority, so it will eventually win. This prevents large-vehicle simulators from monopolising lanes over smaller ones.

docs.title: Branch Weights
docs.text: By default, when a vehicle reaches the end of its current lane and has multiple NextLanes to choose from, the next lane is picked uniformly at random. Branch weights let you bias that choice.

docs.title: Configuring in the Inspector
docs.text:
Each RandomTrafficSimulatorConfiguration exposes a branchWeights array (entries with an unassigned lane or a weight ≤ 0 are ignored):

BranchWeightSet:
  fromLane: Lane_A1
  next:
    - nextLane: Lane_B1,  weight: 2.0
    - nextLane: Lane_B2,  weight: 1.0

In the example above, vehicles leaving Lane_A1 will choose Lane_B1 approximately twice as often as Lane_B2.

docs.title: Configuring via JSON
docs.text:
Branch weights can also be loaded from Assets/Configs/traffic_spawn.json (managed by TrafficSpawnConfig), which makes it easy to iterate without reopening the Unity Editor:

{
  "branchWeights": [
    {
      "fromLane": "Lane_A1",
      "next": [
        { "lane": "Lane_B1", "weight": 2.0 },
        { "lane": "Lane_B2", "weight": 1.0 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Weights are normalised automatically; only their ratios matter.

Branch weights are global

  • Branch weights are stored in the static TrafficSpawnConfig, keyed by fromLane. They apply to every NPC vehicle choosing a next lane from that lane, regardless of which simulator spawned it. If two simulators define the same fromLane, the later entry wins.
  • When a spawn config JSON is loaded, its branchWeights replace the Inspector branch weights.
  • With several TrafficManagers, the last one to initialize (or load a config) defines the weights.
  • Next lanes that have no weight are never chosen while at least one listed lane is available. If none of the listed lanes is among the current NextLanes, the choice falls back to uniform.

docs.title: Per-Lane Spawn Rates
docs.text:
Each lane entry has a spawnsPerMinute field. TrafficManager converts this to a minimum interval between spawns on that lane:

\[ \text{interval} = \frac{60}{\text{spawnsPerMinute}} \text{ seconds} \]

If spawnsPerMinute = 0, there is no rate limit and vehicles spawn as fast as the lane clears.

Maximum rate, not a guaranteed rate

spawnsPerMinute is a cap: it enforces a minimum interval between spawns on that lane. The observed rate is usually lower, because the lane is picked at random among the simulator's lanes and a spawn also needs free space at the spawn point, fewer than maxVehicleCount vehicles, and enough distance to the ego vehicle.

Spawn rates can also be loaded from the same JSON file:

{
  "spawnRates": [
    { "lane": "Lane_A1", "spawnsPerMinute": 6.0 },
    { "lane": "Lane_B2", "spawnsPerMinute": 3.5 }
  ]
}

docs.title: RandomTrafficSimulatorConfiguration Fields
docs.text: Field Description npcPrefabs Array of vehicle prefabs to spawn randomly spawnableLanes SpawnableLaneConfig entries: lane + optional spawnsPerMinute branchWeights Weighted next-lane preferences per lane maximumSpawns Total spawns before this simulator stops (0 = unlimited) enabled Toggle the entire simulator on/off

docs.title: How Vehicles Navigate
docs.text:
Once spawned, an NPC vehicle is handed off to NPCVehicleSimulator, which runs the Cognition → Decision → Control pipeline each FixedUpdate. Route extension works as follows:

flowchart TD
    A[Vehicle reaches end of lane] --> B{Next lanes available?}
    B -- Yes --> C[TrafficSpawnConfig.ChooseNextLane: weighted or uniform]
    B -- No --> D[Mark for despawn]
    C --> E[Continue driving]

See TrafficManager for details on the full simulation pipeline.

docs.title: Adding a New RandomTrafficSimulator
docs.text:
1. Open the TrafficManager component in the Inspector.
  2. Expand the Random Traffic Sims array and add a new entry.
  3. Assign NPC prefabs and spawnable lanes.
  4. Optionally configure branch weights or set a spawnsPerMinute per lane.
  5. Optionally save the configuration to JSON using the Save Spawn Config JSON context menu on TrafficManager.

Tip

You can have multiple RandomTrafficSimulator entries targeting different sets of lanes — for example, one for main roads and another for side streets with lower density.

docs.title: Traffic Manager System
docs.text:
Overview

The Traffic Manager is the central orchestrator for all NPC vehicle simulation. It manages multiple traffic simulators, controls spawn rate and density, enforces ego-vehicle safety distances, and handles the full lifecycle of NPC vehicles — from instantiation to despawn.

docs.title: Core Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    TM[TrafficManager] --> RTS[RandomTrafficSimulator ×N]
    TM --> ROTS[RouteTrafficSimulator ×N]
    TM --> NS[NPCVehicleSimulator]
    NS --> COG[Cognition Step]
    NS --> DEC[Decision Step]
    NS --> CTR[Control Step]
    NS --> VIS[Visualization Step]
    TM --> TSC[TrafficSpawnConfig]
    TSC --> JSON[(traffic_spawn.json)]

docs.title: System Components
docs.text:
Traffic SimulatorsNPC Vehicle SimulatorTrafficSpawnConfig

The manager supports two simulator types running simultaneously:

  • RandomTrafficSimulator — spawns vehicles randomly across a set of lanes, with optional per-lane rates and branch weights. See Random Traffic.
  • RouteTrafficSimulator — spawns vehicles that follow a fixed multi-lane route.

Both implement ITrafficSimulator, giving the manager a uniform interface for spawn requests.

The core physics engine that steps all active NPC vehicles each FixedUpdate:

graph LR
    A[Cognition] --> B[Decision]
    B --> C[Control]
    C --> D[Visualization]

The cognition step uses Unity Job System parallel jobs (IJobParallelFor) and batched physics queries (RaycastCommand / BoxcastCommand) for ground, obstacle and curve checks.

A static configuration layer filled from Assets/Configs/traffic_spawn.json (or from the Inspector data when the file is missing). It holds the branch weights used by the next-lane choice of every NPC vehicle and records branch-decision statistics. Per-lane spawn rates are enforced by TrafficManager itself. See TrafficSpawnConfig.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Field Default Description seed 0 Seed for Unity's random generator. Random.InitState(seed) is called at the start of every initialization, so the same seed reproduces the same random choices (prefabs, spawn lanes, branch decisions) as long as the scene is otherwise deterministic.

Setting the seed

  • Inspector: seed field on the TrafficManager component.
  • JSON configuration (passed on the command line in player builds, or via useJsonConfig in the Editor): the RandomTrafficSeed key of the AutowareSimulation configuration file is written to TrafficManager.seed (and MaxVehicleCount to maxVehicleCount) in Awake, before the manager initializes.
  • Script: Restart(newSeed, newMaxVehicleCount) (see Restart).

If unset, a dummy is created automatically. trafficLanesObject — Parent GameObject containing all TrafficLane components. If unset, the manager falls back to GameObject.Find("TrafficLanes"). If neither exists, an error is logged and lane verification is skipped.
