docs.title: Spawn Configuration (JSON)
docs.text: TrafficManager can save and load a JSON file that controls per-lane spawn rates and branch weights. This makes it easy to tune traffic density without reopening the Unity Editor.

docs.title: Context Menu Actions
docs.text:
Right-click on the TrafficManager component in the Inspector:

  • Save Spawn Config JSON — writes current rates/weights from all simulators to the JSON file.
  • Load Spawn Config JSON — reads the JSON file and applies it to all simulators.

The config is also loaded automatically at scene start if the file exists (otherwise a warning is logged and the Inspector values are used). At runtime, SetSpawnConfigPath(path) changes the path and loads it immediately; the Traffic Settings UI (TrafficSettingsUI) uses GetSpawnConfigPath() / SetSpawnConfigPath() for this.

Player builds

A relative path is resolved against Application.dataPath/... In a player build that is the build folder, so the default file must be copied to <build folder>/Assets/Configs/traffic_spawn.json (or use an absolute path).

What a loaded file overrides

  • branchWeights from the file replace the Inspector branch weights of every random traffic simulator.
  • spawnRates overwrite spawnsPerMinute only for lanes listed in the file. Rate limiting is rebuilt from the file, so spawnable lanes not listed in it are not rate-limited while that file is loaded.
  • TrafficSpawnConfig is static: with several TrafficManagers, the last one to initialize or load defines the global branch weights.

docs.title: JSON Format
docs.text:
{
  "spawnRates": [
    { "lane": "Lane_A1", "spawnsPerMinute": 6.0 },
    { "lane": "Lane_B2", "spawnsPerMinute": 3.5 }
  ],
  "branchWeights": [
    {
      "fromLane": "Lane_A1",
      "next": [
        { "lane": "Lane_B1", "weight": 2.0 },
        { "lane": "Lane_B2", "weight": 1.0 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  • Lane names are case-insensitive.
  • spawnsPerMinute = 0 disables rate limiting for that lane.
  • Weights are normalised automatically; only ratios matter.

docs.title: Per-Lane Rate Limiting
docs.text:
When a spawn rate is set for a lane, TrafficManager tracks the last spawn time per lane and skips spawn attempts until the interval has elapsed:

\[ \text{interval (s)} = \frac{60}{\text{spawnsPerMinute}} \]

Maximum rate, not a guaranteed rate

spawnsPerMinute only enforces a minimum interval between spawns on a lane. The actual rate is usually lower, because each frame a simulator picks one of its lanes at random and the spawn also requires a free spawn area, maxVehicleCount not reached, and enough distance to the ego vehicle.

docs.title: RemoveVehiclesInRadius
docs.text:
The Teleporter (and the ScenarioSelector) call this method before moving the ego vehicle to its new spawn position. All NPC vehicles within radius metres of center are marked for despawn and removed on the next FixedUpdate.

// By world position
int count = trafficManager.RemoveVehiclesInRadius(position, radius);

// By transform
int count = trafficManager.RemoveVehiclesInRadius(transform, radius);

Returns the number of vehicles removed.

docs.title: Fixed Update Cycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant TM as TrafficManager
    participant TS as Traffic Simulators
    participant NS as NPCVehicleSimulator

    TM->>TS: GetRandomSpawnInfo() for each enabled simulator
    TS-->>TM: spawnPoint + prefab
    TM->>TM: Group by spawn point
    TM->>TM: Filter: ego proximity check
    TM->>TM: Filter: per-lane rate limit
    TM->>TM: Collision check (IsSpawnable)
    TM->>TS: Spawn() (checks maximumSpawns, maxVehicleCount)
    TS->>NS: Register new vehicle
    TM->>NS: StepOnce(deltaTime)
    NS->>NS: Cognition → Decision → Control → Visualization
    TM->>TM: Despawn marked vehicles

docs.title: Spawn Decision Logic
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Spawn request] --> B{Distance to ego ≥ spawnDistanceToEgo?}
    B -- No --> SKIP[Skip this frame]
    B -- Yes --> C{Rate limit elapsed?}
    C -- No --> SKIP
    C -- Yes --> D{Single simulator on lane?}
    D -- Yes --> E[IsSpawnable check]
    D -- No --> F[Priority sort → highest wins]
    F --> E
    E -- Clear --> H{Vehicle count < maxVehicleCount?}
    E -- Blocked --> SKIP
    H -- Yes --> G[Spawn vehicle]
    H -- No --> SKIP

A RandomTrafficSimulator is only queried while it is enabled, has at least one valid spawnable lane, and has not reached maximumSpawns. A simulator whose spawnable lanes are all unassigned is treated as disabled.

docs.title: Step 1 — Cognition
docs.text:
Uses Unity Job System jobs and batched physics queries. Each vehicle gathers:

  • Ground existence (vehicle must be above valid surface)
  • Next lane and waypoint
  • Traffic light state and passability
  • Right-of-way at intersections
  • Curve detection (upcoming sharp turns → reduce speed)
  • Front obstacle distance
  • Occupied zebra crossings ahead, via ZebraCrossingArea.TryGetBlockedStop() (see Zebra Crossing)

docs.title: Step 2 — Decision
docs.text:
Determines each vehicle's immediate action:

Speed Mode Trigger NORMAL Open road, green light SLOW Approaching curve or distant obstacle STOP Red light, pedestrian crossing, intersection yield SUDDEN_STOP Close obstacle, blocked crossing ABSOLUTE_STOP Emergency physics limit

The decision step takes the minimum of the stop distances for the front vehicle, traffic light, right-of-way and an occupied zebra crossing (computed in the cognition step) and picks the speed mode from it. See Zebra Crossing.

docs.title: Step 3 — Control
docs.text:
Updates vehicle kinematics:

  • Speed adjusted toward target via acceleration/deceleration ramp
  • Steering computed from angle to next waypoint
  • Position and rotation applied to the Unity transform

docs.title: Step 4 — Visualization
docs.text:
• Applies computed transform to the NPC GameObject
  • Updates turn signal state based on upcoming lane

docs.title: Traffic Light Integration
docs.text:
Follows the Vienna Convention:

State NPC Behaviour 🟢 Green Proceed normally 🟡 Yellow Stop if distance allows; otherwise commit 🔴 Red Stop at stop line

Yellow light decision:

if distance_to_light < sudden_stop_distance:
    commit (cannot stop safely)
else:
    stop

docs.title: Intersection Right-of-Way
docs.text:
NPC vehicles use a yield phase system at intersections:

Phase Meaning NONE Not yielding ENTERING_INTERSECTION Approaching an intersection; evaluating whether to yield (no stop) AT_INTERSECTION Inside the intersection; evaluating whether to yield (no stop) LANES_RULES_ENTERING_INTERSECTION / LANES_RULES_AT_INTERSECTION Yielding based on the lanes' right-of-way rules LEFT_HAND_RULE_ENTERING_INTERSECTION / LEFT_HAND_RULE_AT_INTERSECTION Yielding under the left-hand rule to another nearby vehicle INTERSECTION_BLOCKED Waiting before entering because the intersection is busy FORCING_PRIORITY Yielding inside the intersection to a vehicle that is forcing its priority

docs.title: Initialization (Start)
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Start] --> S["Random.InitState(seed)"]
    S --> B[Build config from Inspector; load spawn config JSON if it exists]
    B --> T[TrafficSpawnConfig.Load]
    T --> G[Set up ego vehicle reference / dummy ego]
    G --> C[Create NPCVehicleSimulator]
    C --> D[verifyIntegrationEnvironmentElements]
    D --> E[Instantiate RandomTrafficSimulators]
    E --> F[Instantiate RouteTrafficSimulators]

A missing lanes parent does not stop initialization (only the lane verification is skipped). If the manager is not initialized (simulator list not created), FixedUpdate logs an error and returns instead of throwing.

docs.title: Restart
docs.text:
trafficManager.Restart(newSeed: 42, newMaxVehicleCount: 20);

Disposes all current state, sets seed and maxVehicleCount, and re-runs initialization (including reloading the spawn config). Both parameters have defaults (newSeed = 0, newMaxVehicleCount = 10), so omitted arguments reset those values rather than keeping the current ones.

docs.title: Destroy
docs.text: On OnDestroy, the manager first disposes the NPCVehicleSimulator, then calls TrafficSpawnConfig.ExportBranchDecisionCsv() to write the branch decision statistics to Assets/Configs/traffic_branch_decisions.csv (relative to the project root). Export errors are logged as warnings. See TrafficSpawnConfig for the CSV format.

docs.title: Scene Setup Checklist
docs.text:
Required before Play

  • [ ] The lanes parent is assigned to trafficLanesObject, or a GameObject named TrafficLanes exists in the scene.
  • [ ] All TrafficLane child objects have unique names.
  • [ ] At least one TrafficLane has intersectionLane = true.
  • [ ] TrafficManager.vehicleLayerMask and groundLayerMask are assigned.
  • [ ] At least one RandomTrafficSimulatorConfiguration entry is configured, with its spawnable lanes assigned.

The first three items are validated at startup (verifyIntegrationEnvironmentElements); errors appear in the Console with descriptive messages.

Upgrading older scenes

spawnableLanes changed from a plain TrafficLane[] to SpawnableLaneConfig entries ({lane, spawnsPerMinute}). Scenes saved with the old format show empty lanes and must be relinked in the Inspector; until then the simulator has no valid spawn lane and is treated as disabled.

docs.title: Extensibility
docs.text:
Custom simulators can be added at runtime via:

trafficManager.AddTrafficSimulator(new MyCustomSimulator(...));

Any class implementing ITrafficSimulator integrates automatically with the priority system and spawn loop.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
TrafficSpawnConfig is a static utility that loads traffic configuration from a JSON file and makes it available to the traffic simulation system at runtime. It controls two things:

  1. Per-lane spawn rates — the maximum number of vehicles per minute each lane may spawn (enforced by TrafficManager).
  2. Branch weights — the probability of NPC vehicles turning onto each downstream lane.

The state is static and global: it is shared by all TrafficManagers, and the last one to initialize (or load a config) wins.

It also records every lane-change decision made during a simulation run and exports them as a CSV on session end, allowing you to verify that configured probabilities match observed behaviour.

docs.title: The JSON Configuration File
docs.text:
Default path: Assets/Configs/traffic_spawn.json

This path is configurable on the TrafficManager component (spawnConfigPath field) and at runtime from the Traffic Settings UI. A relative path is resolved against the project root (Application.dataPath/..); an absolute path is used as-is. The file is loaded automatically at scene start if it exists; otherwise a warning is logged and the Inspector values of the random traffic simulators are used.

Player builds

In a player build, Application.dataPath/.. is the build folder, so the default file must be placed at <build folder>/Assets/Configs/traffic_spawn.json (or an absolute path must be set).

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
{
  "spawnRates": [
    { "lane": "Lane_MainRoad_A",  "spawnsPerMinute": 8.0 },
    { "lane": "Lane_MainRoad_B",  "spawnsPerMinute": 6.0 },
    { "lane": "Lane_SideStreet",  "spawnsPerMinute": 2.0 }
  ],
  "branchWeights": [
    {
      "fromLane": "Lane_MainRoad_A",
      "next": [
        { "lane": "Lane_MainRoad_B",  "weight": 3.0 },
        { "lane": "Lane_SideStreet",  "weight": 1.0 }
      ]
    },
    {
      "fromLane": "Lane_MainRoad_B",
      "next": [
        { "lane": "Lane_MainRoad_A",  "weight": 1.0 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: spawnRates
docs.text:
Field Type Description lane string Lane GameObject name (compared case-insensitively). spawnsPerMinute float Maximum spawn frequency: enforces a minimum interval of 60 / spawnsPerMinute s between spawns on this lane. It is not a guaranteed rate. 0 disables rate limiting for this lane.

Only spawnable lanes listed in the file get a rate limit while the file is loaded; unlisted lanes are not rate-limited.

docs.title: branchWeights
docs.text:
Field Type Description fromLane string The lane where vehicles are making a turn decision (case-insensitive). next[].lane string Name of a downstream lane option. next[].weight float Relative probability weight. Values are normalised automatically; entries with weight ≤ 0 are ignored.

Branch weights from the file replace the Inspector branchWeights of every random traffic simulator.

Normalisation

Weights do not need to sum to 1. The system normalises them internally. A weight of 2.0 for lane B and 1.0 for lane C means B is chosen 67% of the time.

docs.title: Saving and Loading from TrafficManager
docs.text:
The TrafficManager Inspector provides two context menu actions:

Action Effect Save Spawn Config JSON Reads current spawn rates and branch weights from all RandomTrafficSimulator entries and writes them to the JSON file. Load Spawn Config JSON Reads the JSON file and applies spawn rates and branch weights back to all simulators.

You can also call these at runtime:

trafficManager.SetSpawnConfigPath("Assets/Configs/my_config.json");  // loads immediately
trafficManager.SaveSpawnConfigJson();
trafficManager.LoadSpawnConfigJson();

Note

Every load (TrafficSpawnConfig.Load, including SetSpawnConfigPath, Load Spawn Config JSON and Restart) clears the branch decision statistics collected so far.

docs.title: Branch Decision Statistics
docs.text:
Every time ChooseNextLane picks a next lane, TrafficSpawnConfig records it internally, aggregated per (from_lane, to_lane, selection_mode). In TrafficManager.OnDestroy() (after the NPC vehicle simulator is disposed), these statistics are written to a CSV file. Export errors are logged as warnings.

Default output path: Assets/Configs/traffic_branch_decisions.csv (relative to the project root). Ratios and averages are written with 6 decimals using the invariant culture (. as decimal separator), independent of the system locale.

docs.title: CSV Column Reference
docs.text: Column Description from_lane Origin lane name to_lane Chosen next lane selection_mode How the lane was chosen (see below) decision_count How many times this transition occurred total_from_lane Total decisions made from this lane (all destinations) total_from_lane_mode Total decisions from this lane using this selection mode observed_ratio_from_lane decision_count / total_from_lane observed_ratio_from_lane_mode decision_count / total_from_lane_mode avg_configured_weight Average configured weight of the chosen lane, after normalisation over all next entries of fromLane in the config. 0 for uniform modes. avg_effective_probability Average probability the chosen lane actually had at decision time: its weight divided by the sum of weights of the configured lanes present in the current NextLanes (weighted), or 1 / NextLanes.Count (uniform modes).

docs.title: Selection Modes
docs.text: Mode Meaning weighted Weights for fromLane matched at least one current next lane and were used uniform_not_loaded No config is loaded — uniform random uniform_no_config Config loaded, but it has no weights for this fromLane uniform_no_matching_weights Weights exist for fromLane, but none of their lanes is in the current NextLanes uniform_weighted_fallback Weighted draw did not select a lane (floating-point rounding edge case) — uniform random

docs.title: Using the CSV
docs.text:
For weighted rows, compare avg_effective_probability against observed_ratio_from_lane_mode to verify that the configured weights produce the expected routing ratios. Over a long run, these should converge. avg_configured_weight equals avg_effective_probability only when all configured next lanes are available.

Example — expected vs. observed for the config { B: 3.0, C: 1.0 } (illustrative values):

to_lane avg_configured_weight avg_effective_probability observed_ratio_from_lane_mode Lane_B 0.75 0.75 0.742 Lane_C 0.25 0.25 0.258

docs.title: Programmatic API
docs.text: Method Description TryGetSpawnRate(laneName, out rate) Query the stored spawn rate for a lane. Not used by spawning (TrafficManager keeps its own per-lane lookup). ChooseNextLane(fromLane, options) Weighted random selection from a list of next lanes (records the decision) ExportBranchDecisionCsv(path = null) Write the decision statistics CSV immediately; returns the full path Load(ConfigData) / Load(jsonPath) Load from a pre-parsed config object or a JSON file (clears previous state and statistics) ReadJson(path) Parse a JSON file and return a ConfigData object (null if missing or invalid) VerboseBranchLogging Static flag, false by default. When true, every weighted decision logs two lines to the Console.

docs.title: Example: Manual Lane Selection
docs.text:
TrafficLane next = TrafficSpawnConfig.ChooseNextLane(currentLane, currentLane.NextLanes);

If no weights are configured for currentLane, the method falls back to uniform random selection transparently.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
Iterate Without Reopening Unity

Edit traffic_spawn.json in any text editor while the project is closed, then use Load Spawn Config JSON from the context menu when you reopen it — or set the path via script and call LoadSpawnConfigJson() at runtime for live reloading.

Start from the Current Setup

Use Save Spawn Config JSON to capture the current Inspector configuration as a JSON baseline, then modify the file from there.

Lane Names Must Be Unique

TrafficManager validates that all TrafficLane objects have unique names. Duplicate names will cause incorrect rate/weight lookup. The validation runs at startup and logs errors to the Console.

docs.title: Adding New Vehicle
docs.text:
Firstly, set up the vehicle based on the tutorial from AWSIM ( Awsim Link )

  1. Create an empty object under the "sensorkit_base_link"" or any other object responsible for sensor data. Name the object "perception_sensor".
  1. Add "Detected Object Autoware" to the "perception_sensor".

  1. Under the "perception_sensor" object, you can add mock sensors in two ways::

    1. Create them from scratch based on our documentation link
    2. Use the prefabs inside the Assets\KashiwaPackage\Prefabs\Pseudo Sensors

  2. You must add a reference to your sensor in the list of sensors within the "Detected Objects Autoware" component.

  1. The Bus Transform must reference the base link of your car for autonomous data capturing to work correctly in the ROS world and for relative data to be captured precisely.

  2. You are also required to add a reference to your sensors in the scenario component as shown in the picture. Be careful when selecting the correct list; you must choose the appropriate list and drag and drop the sensor onto it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This system controls the movement of pedestrians and cyclists along defined paths in the scene. It is built from these cooperating components:

Component Role WaypointSystem Defines an ordered sequence of path points WaypointFollower Moves a character along a WaypointSystem HumanNpcSpawner Pool-based spawner that assigns NPCs to randomly chosen paths SpawnerOnWaypoint Manual or timed spawner for a single path SpawnerOnWaypoint2 Timed spawner that picks a random prefab and a random spawn point / path ScenarioHumanId Assigns a unique ID to each spawned human

JSON-driven paths

Paths can also be defined in a JSON file instead of being placed by hand. In the NormalTraffics scenario of the Kashiwa scene, pedestrians and cyclists are spawned this way by PedestrianCyclistSpawner. See Path Spawn Config (JSON).

docs.title: WaypointSystem
docs.text: This component should be added to a parent GameObject. Child Transform objects define the waypoint positions in sequence.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Create a parent GameObject (e.g., Path_Sidewalk_A).
  2. Add child Transform objects at each waypoint position.
  3. Add the WaypointSystem component to the parent.
  4. Click Clear Waypoints, then Generate Waypoints from Children — this populates the list in order.

If Gizmos are enabled, the path is drawn as:

  • Spheres at the waypoints
  • Green lines connecting consecutive waypoints
  • A closing line from last to first when loopStatus = true

Empty (None) waypoint slots are skipped when drawing the gizmos, so a half-edited list does not throw errors in the Scene view. At runtime, however, every slot must reference a Transform.

Green line in the Scene view and WaypointSystem in the Inspector.

docs.title: Key Properties and Methods
docs.text: Member Description loopStatus When true, the follower wraps from the last waypoint back to the first. When false, the follower is deactivated at the last waypoint (returned to the pool) GetFirstWaypoint() Returns the first waypoint Transform GetClosestWaypoint(position) Finds the nearest WaypointNode to a world position GetClosestWaypointIndex(position) Returns the index of the nearest waypoint GetNextWaypointIndex(index) Returns (index + 1) % count GetWaypointByIndex(index) Direct index access GenerateWaypointsFromChildren() Auto-populates the list from child transforms EndPathCheck(index) Returns true when index == count - 1

docs.title: WaypointFollower
docs.text:
By adding a WaypointFollower component to a pedestrian or cyclist, it will automatically navigate toward successive waypoints in the assigned WaypointSystem.

Assign the target path via the waypointSystem field in the Inspector, or from code:

Method Description SetWaypointSystem(ws) Assigns the path and starts from the waypoint closest to the current position ForceStartAtFirstWaypoint() Teleports the character to the first waypoint and starts from index 0

When a non-looping path ends (or the character falls below y = -200), the follower stops the rigidbody and calls SetActive(false) on its GameObject, so spawners can reuse it.

Pedestrian NPC with a WaypointFollower component assigned.

docs.title: IConstraintWayPoint
docs.text:
IConstraintWayPoint is an interface for adding stopping conditions at specific waypoints — for example, stopping at a red light before crossing the road.

Constraint components are evaluated when the follower reaches the waypoint they are attached to (the follower waits there until all constraints pass), so place traffic-light constraints just before the crossing point.

Provided implementations:

Class Description ConstraintPedestrianTrafficLight Stop unless the pedestrian signal is green ConstraintCarTrafficLight Stop when vehicle signal is red ConstraintSaftyDistance Stop when a vehicle is too close

Traffic light constraint attached to a waypoint before the crossing.

docs.title: HumanNpcSpawner
docs.text: HumanNpcSpawner manages a pool of human NPCs and spawns them throughout a simulation run. It is designed for crowd scenes where many pedestrians need to be maintained without manual placement.

docs.title: Spawn Behaviour
docs.text:
1. On Start, every NPC in HumanPool is deactivated.
  2. An initial burst of Random.Range(initialSpawnMin, initialSpawnMax + 1) NPCs is spawned.
  3. If runSpawnLoopAfterInitial is true, a coroutine spawns a batch every waitTimeRandomGeneration seconds. The batch size is numberSpawningHuman, plus a random offset in [-varianceSpawningHuman, +varianceSpawningHuman] (minimum 0).
  4. A batch is capped at the number of waypointSystems. Each NPC in a batch gets a different path (paths are not reserved across batches).
  5. Deactivated NPCs from HumanPool are reused first. If the pool is short, up to maxExtraInstantiatesPerCycle clones of random pool members are created and added to HumanPool.
  6. Each NPC is placed at the first waypoint of its path (ForceStartAtFirstWaypoint), gets a new ScenarioHumanId, and is activated.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Default Description HumanPool — Human NPC instances (each must have a WaypointFollower). All are deactivated on start waypointSystems — All available WaypointSystem paths initialSpawnMin / initialSpawnMax 0 / 5 Inclusive range for the one-time initial burst runSpawnLoopAfterInitial true If false, only the initial burst is spawned waitTimeRandomGeneration 5 Seconds between spawn batches numberSpawningHuman 3 NPCs per batch varianceSpawningHuman 0 Random ± variation of the batch size maxExtraInstantiatesPerCycle 10 Max clones created per batch when the pool is short activeParent — Optional parent for activated NPCs

Public methods: TriggerNow() runs one batch immediately; RestartLoop() restarts the spawn coroutine (e.g. after changing waitTimeRandomGeneration).

Pool Reuse

When an NPC reaches the end of a non-looping path, WaypointFollower deactivates it. It stays in HumanPool and becomes available on the next spawn cycle.

docs.title: SpawnerOnWaypoint
docs.text: SpawnerOnWaypoint is a lighter-weight spawner for scenario-specific placements. It instantiates spawnerPrefab at the pose of initialSapwnPoint (captured in Awake), either on a key press or on a random timer, and assigns it to waypointSystem. Spawned objects are parented to the spawner and are not pooled.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Default Description initialSapwnPoint — Transform whose position/rotation is used for spawning spawnerPrefab — Prefab to instantiate (must have a WaypointFollower) waypointSystem — Path the spawned object will follow (starts from the waypoint closest to the spawn point) spawnRandomEnable false Enable automatic timed spawning minWaitingTime / maxWaitingTime 5 / 300 Random interval range (seconds) for timed spawning spawnKey KeyCode.O Manual spawn key

docs.title: SpawnerOnWaypoint2
docs.text:
SpawnerOnWaypoint2 spawns on a random timer only (no key). Each time the timer expires, it picks a random prefab from prefabPool and a random entry from spawnPoints; each SpawnPoint holds one WaypointSystem and a list of preferred spawn transforms, one of which is chosen at random.

Field Default Description spawnPoints — List of SpawnPoint (waypointSystem + preferred spawn transforms) prefabPool — Prefabs to choose from (must have a WaypointFollower) spawnRandomEnable true Enable timed spawning minWaitingTime / maxWaitingTime 5 / 50 Random interval range (seconds)

Tip

Use SpawnerOnWaypoint / SpawnerOnWaypoint2 when you need a pedestrian to appear at a specific place or scenario moment. Use HumanNpcSpawner, or the JSON-driven PedestrianCyclistSpawner, for continuous background crowd generation.

docs.title: ScenarioHumanId
docs.text:
ScenarioHumanId holds a globally unique sequential integer ID (as a string) for a human NPC.

A new ID is assigned every time an NPC is (re)activated or spawned, so a pooled NPC that is reused gets a different ID on each trip. IDs are assigned by:

  • HumanNpcSpawner
  • SpawnerOnWaypoint and SpawnerOnWaypoint2
  • The JSON path spawners (PedestrianCyclistSpawner, PedestrianPathSpawner, CyclistPathSpawner)
  • Ros2EntityController (pedestrians spawned over ROS 2)

Each of these adds the component if it is missing. Humans placed directly in the scene (not spawned) get one lazily from LogArea the first time they are logged.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The ID is used by the LogArea system to uniquely identify each pedestrian across CSV rows, even if multiple pedestrians are in the scene at the same time.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
var idComp = npc.GetComponent<ScenarioHumanId>();
idComp.AssignNewId();       // assigns the next available ID
string id = idComp.HumanId; // "0", "1", "2", ...

IDs are sequential and restart from 0 each time Unity enters Play mode. The DisallowMultipleComponent attribute ensures only one ID component per NPC.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Zebra Crossing system makes NPC vehicles automatically yield to pedestrians and cyclists at crosswalks. It consists of two components:

  • ZebraCrossingArea — attached to an individual crosswalk trigger. Detects occupants and exposes a static query API for NPC vehicles.
  • ZebraCrossingConfig — optional parent component. Defines a shared whitelist of occupant types for all child ZebraCrossingArea objects.

docs.title: Full Interaction Pipeline
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Pedestrian / Cyclist
    participant ZA as ZebraCrossingArea (Trigger)
    participant CS as NPCVehicleCognitionStep
    participant ST as NPCVehicleInternalState
    participant DS as NPCVehicleDecisionStep

    P->>ZA: OnTriggerEnter
    ZA->>ZA: Add root to occupantRoots (if whitelisted)

    Note over CS: Every FixedUpdate — after ground/obstacle jobs complete
    CS->>ZA: TryGetBlockedStop(frontCenterPos, forward)
    ZA-->>CS: blocked=true, distance=12.3m, area="CrosswalkNorth"
    CS->>ST: IsZebraBlocked = true
    CS->>ST: DistanceToZebraStop = 12.3
    CS->>ST: ZebraAreaName = "CrosswalkNorth"
    CS->>ST: WasZebraBlocked = true

    Note over DS: Same FixedUpdate — after Cognition
    DS->>ST: Read IsZebraBlocked, DistanceToZebraStop
    DS->>DS: distanceToStop = Min(frontVehicle, trafficLight, rightOfWay, zebraStop)
    DS->>ST: SpeedMode = STOP (or SUDDEN_STOP / ABSOLUTE_STOP)

    P->>ZA: OnTriggerExit (or occupant destroyed / deactivated)
    ZA->>ZA: Remove root from occupantRoots
    CS->>ZA: TryGetBlockedStop → blocked=false
    CS->>ST: IsZebraBlocked = false
    CS->>ST: WasZebraBlocked = false
    DS->>ST: SpeedMode follows the remaining stop conditions

The zebra occupancy is evaluated in the cognition step; the decision step only consumes the stored distance.

docs.title: Where the Code Lives
docs.text: Code location What it does ZebraCrossingArea.OnTriggerEnter/Exit Maintains the set of current occupants ZebraCrossingArea.IsOccupied Drops occupants that were destroyed or deactivated inside the trigger (they never receive OnTriggerExit) NPCVehicleCognitionStep.UpdateZebraCrossingAwareness() Queries every active area for every NPC vehicle each FixedUpdate NPCVehicleInternalState fields Stores the result between Cognition and Decision steps NPCVehicleDecisionStep.UpdateSpeedMode() Includes DistanceToZebraStop in the minimum stop distance calculation

docs.title: NPC Vehicle State Fields
docs.text:
These fields are written by the Cognition step and read by the Decision step each frame:

Field Type Description IsZebraBlocked bool True when a blocked crossing is detected ahead DistanceToZebraStop float Distance to the stop point (metres), float.MaxValue if not blocked ZebraAreaName string Name of the matched ZebraCrossingArea, null if not blocked WasZebraBlocked bool Previous frame's value — used to log the first frame of a stop

All fields are reset at the start of every cognition update and re-filled only if a blocked crossing is found.

docs.title: How the Stop Distance Is Used
docs.text:
In NPCVehicleDecisionStep, the zebra stop distance competes with all other stop conditions:

var distanceToStopPointByZebra = state.IsZebraBlocked
    ? state.DistanceToZebraStop
    : float.MaxValue;

var distanceToStopPoint = Mathf.Min(
    distanceToStopPointByFrontVehicle,
    distanceToStopPointByTrafficLight,
    distanceToStopPointByRightOfWay,
    distanceToStopPointByZebra        // ← zebra crossing
);

The resulting distanceToStopPoint then determines the speed mode:

Condition Speed Mode distance ≤ absoluteStopDistance ABSOLUTE_STOP distance ≤ suddenStopDistance SUDDEN_STOP distance ≤ stopDistance STOP distance ≤ slowDownDistance or vehicle is turning SLOW otherwise NORMAL

Where the distances depend on current speed and the deceleration values in NPCVehicleConfig:

\[ d_\text{stoppable} = \frac{v^2}{2 \cdot a} \]

plus a fixed margin (MinStopDistance = 1.5 m: ×1 for absolute, ×2 for sudden, ×3 for normal stop; slowDownDistance = stopDistance + 4 × 1.5 m).

So a faster NPC vehicle needs more distance to stop and may enter SUDDEN_STOP or ABSOLUTE_STOP if the crossing is detected late.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Create an empty GameObject positioned over the crosswalk.
  2. Add a Collider component and enable Is Trigger.
  3. Scale the collider to cover the full crossing surface.
  4. Attach the ZebraCrossingArea script.
  5. Assign a Stop Point transform — place this just before the stop line where vehicles should halt.

Rigidbody required

Unity only sends trigger events if the occupant or the area has a Rigidbody (kinematic is fine). Without one, occupants are never detected.

One stop point per approach direction

Each area has a single stop point, and detection is purely geometric (distance and angle to the stop point, no lane matching). An area therefore serves one approach direction; for a two-way road, add one area with its own stop point per direction.

docs.title: Occupant Detection
docs.text:
The area automatically identifies the following types:

Type Detection method NPCPedestrian GetComponentInParent<NPCPedestrian>() SimpleCyclistMovement Full type name match on a MonoBehaviour in the parent hierarchy BicycleMoveRotate Full type name match on a MonoBehaviour in the parent hierarchy V2X.Paths.ClearWaypointFollower Full type name match on a MonoBehaviour in the parent hierarchy WaypointFollower (global namespace) Full type name match on a MonoBehaviour in the parent hierarchy

The occupant's root transform (transform.root) is stored, not the collider's transform, so compound colliders on a single character count as one occupant. Occupants parented under a common scene object share that root and therefore count as a single occupant.

docs.title: Whitelist Filtering
docs.text:
If a ZebraCrossingConfig parent is present with non-empty lists, only occupants matching the whitelist are counted:

  • allowedPrefabs — exact match of the normalized names ((Clone), (clone), _clone, _Clone removed, then trimmed).
  • allowedRootNameSubstrings — case-insensitive substring of the normalized root name.

If both lists are empty, all detected types are allowed.

docs.title: Inspector Fields
docs.text: Field Default Description stopPoint This object Transform where vehicles should stop. Defaults to the area's own position if unset. maxDetectionDistance 40 m How far ahead a vehicle will look for this crossing forwardAngleTolerance 80° Angular cone (half-angle) in front of vehicle for detection stopBuffer 1.5 m Extra gap kept between the vehicle and the stop point enableDebugLogs false Log occupancy changes, ignored colliders and stop decisions to the Console

docs.title: Static Query API
docs.text:
It is called once per FixedUpdate by the cognition step for every NPC vehicle not marked for despawn:

bool blocked = ZebraCrossingArea.TryGetBlockedStop(
    vehiclePosition,   // vehicle's front-center world position
    vehicleForward,    // vehicle's forward direction (Y is ignored)
    out float distance,           // distance to the stop point (minus buffer)
    out ZebraCrossingArea area    // the matched area, or null
);

The method checks all active, occupied ZebraCrossingArea instances and returns the closest one that:

  1. Has its stop point within maxDetectionDistance (horizontal distance)
  2. Has its stop point within the forwardAngleTolerance cone in front of the vehicle

distance is the horizontal distance to the stop point minus stopBuffer, clamped to ≥ 0. If blocked == true, the cognition step stores it in DistanceToZebraStop; the decision step then includes it in the minimum stop distance, which yields STOP, SUDDEN_STOP or ABSOLUTE_STOP (or SLOW while still far away) depending on speed.

docs.title: Gizmo Visualization
docs.text:
When the GameObject is selected in the Scene view:

  • Green wireframe — crossing is clear (no occupants)
  • Red wireframe — crossing is occupied
  • Cyan sphere — stop point position

Enable enableDebugLogs to see occupant enter/exit events in the Console, plus an NPC-level message when a vehicle starts stopping:

[NPC Zebra] Vehicle 'Bus_01' stopping for zebra 'CrosswalkNorth' at ~12.3m.

This message fires on the first frame an NPC detects the blocking state (WasZebraBlocked transition false → true). The code also contains a "cleared zebra" message, but it never fires in the current implementation (ZebraAreaName is reset to null before the check), so nothing is logged when the crossing clears.

Note

With enableDebugLogs on, TryGetBlockedStop also logs a [ZebraCrossingArea] Blocked ... line for every vehicle matching the area, every frame — use it only for short debugging sessions.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Place this component on a parent GameObject that groups multiple ZebraCrossingArea children. All child areas inherit its whitelist settings.

ZebraCrossingConfig (parent)
├── ZebraCrossingArea (north crosswalk)
├── ZebraCrossingArea (south crosswalk)
└── ZebraCrossingArea (east crosswalk)

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Description allowedPrefabs Only occupants whose root name matches one of these prefab names are counted allowedRootNameSubstrings Only occupants whose root name contains one of these strings (case-insensitive) are counted

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
allowedRootNameSubstrings: ["Human", "Cyclist", "Pedestrian"]

This ensures that vehicles that enter the trigger zone accidentally (e.g., due to overlapping colliders) are not counted as occupants.

docs.title: Complete Setup Example
docs.text:
Intersection (GameObject)
└── ZebraCrossingConfig
    ├── allowedRootNameSubstrings: ["Human", "Bicycle"]
    │
    ├── CrosswalkNorth (GameObject)
    │   ├── BoxCollider [Is Trigger = true]
    │   ├── ZebraCrossingArea
    │   │   └── stopPoint → StopLineNorth (Transform)
    │   └── StopLineNorth (child Transform)
    │
    └── CrosswalkEast (GameObject)
        ├── BoxCollider [Is Trigger = true]
        ├── ZebraCrossingArea
        │   └── stopPoint → StopLineEast (Transform)
        └── StopLineEast (child Transform)

Collider Must Be a Trigger

The ZebraCrossingArea script calls Reset() automatically to set isTrigger = true when first added. If you replace the collider later, make sure to re-enable the trigger flag.

Placement

Place the collider so it covers the full painted area of the crosswalk, not just the curb edge. Pedestrians need to be inside the zone for the system to work correctly.

docs.title: Scenario Configuration
docs.text:
From v3.2 the simulator builds its RSUs, pseudo sensors, publishers, traffic, pedestrians, teleports and raw sensors from YAML files, and sets the ego vehicle, time scale, seed, sun, fog, loggers and signal timing from them, in config/ when Play starts. The Unity scene keeps the map, the roads, the traffic lights and the vehicle and sensor prefabs. To change a scenario you edit the files instead of the scene. You can edit them by hand or in the web viewer Settings tab.

When changes apply

The files are read once, when Play starts (or when a built simulator starts). Saved changes apply on the next run.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text: Page File Sets Simulation simulation.yaml ego vehicle and start pose, time scale, seed, sun, fog, loggers Signal Timing signals.yaml step durations of the traffic signals RSUs and Pseudo Sensors rsus.yaml RSUs, sensors, object-info / Autoware-object / traffic-signal publishers Vehicle Traffic vehicles.yaml spawn points, branch ratios, vehicle types, right of way, removal of stuck vehicles Pedestrians and Cyclists pedestrians.yaml walking and cycling paths, spawn rates, cyclist share Teleports teleports.yaml teleport gates for the ego vehicle Raw Sensors raw_sensors.yaml LiDARs and cameras that publish raw data Sensor Types defaults/sensor_types.yaml pseudo-sensor types (FOV, range) and raw-sensor prefabs Noise Profiles defaults/noise.yaml detection noise Network Profiles defaults/network.yaml delayed / lossy copies (DSRC, Cellular)

docs.title: How to change the configuration
docs.text:
There are three ways. All of them change the same files, so you can mix them.

Way Use it for Web viewer → Settings (tools/web-viewer/run.sh, open http://localhost:8080, top bar Settings) Everyday changes. Lists and forms for every file, with editing on the map. Save checks everything first. See Web Viewer → Settings. Edit the YAML files in config/ with any text editor Many similar changes at once, or with version control. Errors show in the Unity Console as [Config] … when Play starts. Unity menu V2X → Config → Export … Copy what you built in the scene into the files (see Editing in Unity)

After a change, press Play again (or restart the built simulator). To undo, use Reset to default in the web viewer (or copy the file back from config/factory/).

docs.text: Task In the web viewer (Settings) In the files Make a new scenario New… copies the current one; Make default loads it at Play Copy a folder in config/scenarios/, write its name in config/default_scenario.txt (or pick it on the Config Bootstrap object, or start with --scenario <name>) Use the Lexus instead of the bus Simulation → vehicle simulation.yaml → ego.vehicle Start the ego somewhere else Simulation → Place on map, then drag; set heading simulation.yaml → ego.pose Run faster than real time Simulation → time scale simulation.yaml → time_scale Repeat the same traffic Simulation → random seed simulation.yaml → seed Evening, night, fog Simulation → time of day, fog visibility simulation.yaml → lighting.time_of_day, weather.fog_visibility_m Turn CSV logging on or off Simulation → Loggers simulation.yaml → loggers Change a signal cycle Signals → intersection → step durations signals.yaml → steps[].duration_s Add, move or remove an RSU sensor RSUs & sensors → RSU → Place on map / drag / × rsus.yaml → rsus[].sensors Change a sensor's range or field of view RSUs & sensors → sensor → range, h FOV, v FOV (or Defaults → sensor type) rsus.yaml (per sensor) or defaults/sensor_types.yaml (per type) Change sensor noise or network delay Defaults → Noise / Network profiles; RSUs → publisher → noise, network copies defaults/noise.yaml, defaults/network.yaml, rsus.yaml publishers Publish a new object-info topic RSUs & sensors → Object-info publishers → + Add rsus.yaml → object_info_publishers More or less traffic Vehicles → spawn point → vehicles / minute; max vehicles vehicles.yaml → spawn_points, max_vehicles Add a spawn point or a turn ratio Vehicles → click a lane → Spawn vehicles here / Set branch ratios vehicles.yaml → spawn_points, branches Add a pedestrian or cyclist route Pedestrians → + Add, click the points on the map pedestrians.yaml → paths Move or add a teleport gate Teleports → drag the gate / Place gate on map teleports.yaml Switch a LiDAR or camera on or off, change its topic Raw sensors → sensor → enabled, topics raw_sensors.yaml

docs.title: Folder layout
docs.text:
config/
├── default_scenario.txt          name of the scenario that is loaded (one line)
├── defaults/                     shared by all scenarios
│   ├── sensor_types.yaml         pseudo-sensor types (FOV, range) and raw-sensor prefabs
│   ├── noise.yaml                noise profiles
│   └── network.yaml              network profiles (DSRC, Cellular, …)
├── scenarios/
│   └── kashiwa_cool4/
│       ├── scenario.yaml         lists the files of this scenario
│       ├── simulation.yaml       ego vehicle, time scale, seed, sun, fog, loggers
│       ├── signals.yaml          traffic-signal step durations
│       ├── rsus.yaml             RSUs, pseudo sensors, object-info / Autoware / signal publishers
│       ├── vehicles.yaml         NPC vehicle traffic
│       ├── pedestrians.yaml      pedestrian and cyclist paths
│       ├── teleports.yaml        teleport gates for the ego vehicle
│       └── raw_sensors.yaml      LiDARs and cameras that publish raw data
├── maps/traffic_lanes.json       simulator lanes for the web viewer (generated)
└── factory/                      shipped copy of every file ("Reset to default")

scenario.yaml names the files of its scenario. If a key is missing, that part keeps the setup of the scene:

name: kashiwa_cool4
description: exported from V2X_E2E_Simulator_v3.1.1
rsus: rsus.yaml
vehicles: vehicles.yaml
pedestrians: pedestrians.yaml
teleports: teleports.yaml
raw_sensors: raw_sensors.yaml
simulation: simulation.yaml
signals: signals.yaml

docs.title: Choosing the scenario
docs.text:
The first of these that is set is used:

  1. Command-line argument --scenario <name> (built simulator).
  2. The Scenario field of the Config Bootstrap object in the scene.
  3. config/default_scenario.txt.

--config-root <path> reads the configuration from another folder. By default it is config/ next to Assets/ in the editor, and next to the <name>_Data folder in a build.

Errors

The simulator checks all files before it builds anything. If there is an error (a missing file, an unknown sensor type, a duplicate ID, …), it logs every problem in the Console as [Config] …. It then runs with the scene's own setup. The web viewer runs the same checks before it saves.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
Positions use the map frame of Autoware and the Lanelet2 map: MGRS-local x (east) and y (north), and z (height), in metres. These are the coordinates you see in RViz.

Field Meaning x, y, z map frame, metres heading_deg direction the object faces, clockwise from north (0 = north, 90 = east) pitch_deg positive looks up, negative looks down roll_deg roll around the viewing direction

Fields of view (h_fov_deg, v_fov_deg) are full angles. A 60° sensor sees 30° to each side.

docs.title: Editing in Unity
docs.text:
The V2X → Config menu has:

  • Add Config Bootstrap To Scene: adds the object that loads the configuration. It is already in the v3.2 scene.
  • Export Scene To Config: writes the scene's RSUs, sensors and publishers to rsus.yaml and the defaults.
  • Export Vehicle Traffic / Pedestrians And Teleports / Raw Sensors To Config: writes the other files from the scene.
  • Export Simulation And Signal Timing To Config: writes simulation.yaml (the active ego, its pose, sun and loggers of the scene) and signals.yaml.
  • Export Traffic Lanes For The Web Viewer: writes config/maps/traffic_lanes.json. Run it again after you change the lanes in the scene.

Warning

An export overwrites the file it writes, including entries you added by hand.

docs.title: Network Profiles
docs.text:
File config/defaults/network.yaml Web viewer Settings → Defaults Unity export V2X → Config → Export Scene To Config

These defaults are shared by all scenarios.

A network profile publishes a delayed, lossy copy of a topic as <topic><topic_suffix>, for example /v2x/object_info/DSRC. Publishers list the profiles they use under network.

network_profiles:
- name: DSRC
  topic_suffix: /DSRC
  delay_ms: 100
  delay_variance_ms: 0
  packet_loss: 0.05
  packet_loss_variance: 0
  ground_truth: false
Field Meaning delay_ms, delay_variance_ms latency and its random ± part packet_loss, packet_loss_variance probability (0–1) that a message is dropped ground_truth also make a copy of the ground-truth topic

docs.title: Noise Profiles
docs.text:
File config/defaults/noise.yaml Web viewer Settings → Defaults Unity export V2X → Config → Export Scene To Config

These defaults are shared by all scenarios.

noise_profiles:
- name: Default
  distribution: uniform        # uniform | gaussian
  x_m: 0.5
  y_m: 0.5
  z_m: 0.5
  gaussian_mean: 0
  gaussian_std_dev: 25

Publishers refer to a profile by name for each kind of noise: position, rotation, dimension (size) and probability (existence).

Field Meaning distribution uniform: a random value in [−amplitude, +amplitude] per axis. gaussian: gaussian_mean + gaussian_std_dev × amplitude × N(0,1) x_m, y_m, z_m amplitude per axis (m)

NoNoise (all zero) is used for ground truth.

docs.text:
File config/scenarios/<name>/pedestrians.yaml Web viewer Settings → Pedestrians Unity export V2X → Config → Export Pedestrians And Teleports To Config 
max_active: 5                        # agents walking at the same time (0 = unlimited)
snap_to_ground: true
paths:
- id: Path2
  spawns_per_minute: 0.133
  cyclist_ratio: 0.29                # share of cyclists: 0 = only pedestrians, 1 = only cyclists
  enabled: true
  waypoints:
  - {x: 4480.579, y: 72960.906, z: 23}
  - {x: 4487.901, y: 72948.555, z: 23}

docs.title: Raw Sensors
docs.text:
File config/scenarios/<name>/raw_sensors.yaml Web viewer Settings → Raw sensors Unity export V2X → Config → Export Raw Sensors To Config

These are LiDARs (RGL) and cameras that publish point clouds and images.

raw_sensors:
- name: BusAutowareFinal/URDF/base_link/sensor_kit_base_link/velodyne_left_base_link/VelodyneVLP16
  kind: lidar                    # lidar | camera
  mount: ego                     # ego | scene | world
  vehicle: BusAutowareFinal
  object: URDF/base_link/sensor_kit_base_link/velodyne_left_base_link/VelodyneVLP16
  enabled: true
  hz: 10
  frame_id: world
  point_cloud_topics:
  - {topic: lidar_left/pointcloud, format: Pcl24, publish: true}
  - {topic: lidar_left/pointcloud_ex, format: PointXYZIRCAEDT, publish: true}
- name: CameraSensor2
  kind: camera
  mount: scene
  object: AutowareSimulator/Cooperative Autonomous Driving/RSUs/Publishers/Int#2 Raw Sensors/Cameras/CameraSensor2
  enabled: true
  hz: 10
  frame_id: traffic_light_left_camera/camera_optical_link
  image_topic: /rsu/intersection2/camera_2/camera_raw
  camera_info_topic: /rsu/intersection2/camera_2/camera_info
  width: 480
  height: 270
mount Meaning ego a sensor on an ego vehicle (object = path below the vehicle; [i] tells same-named sensors apart) scene a sensor already in the scene (object = scene path) world a new sensor created from a type of raw_sensor_types at pose

Sensors of the scene that are not listed keep their scene setup. Set enabled: false to switch one off.

docs.title: RSUs and Pseudo Sensors
docs.text:
File config/scenarios/<name>/rsus.yaml Web viewer Settings → RSUs & sensors Unity export V2X → Config → Export Scene To Config 
rsus:
- name: Ganken
  rsu_id: 0x12020001      # 32-bit hex, unique; used in object IDs and information_source_list
  location: Ganken
  enabled: true
  sensors:
  - name: RSU_Lidar 1
    type: lidar_60x22deg_60m
    sensor_id: 1          # 0-255, unique within the RSU
    enabled: true
    pose: {x: 4240.481, y: 73444.969, z: 25.433, heading_deg: 35.5, pitch_deg: -13.8, roll_deg: 0}
    # optional: range_m: 80, h_fov_deg: 90, v_fov_deg: 30
    # optional own topics (no network copies):
    # object_info: {topic: /v2x/rsu1/lidar1/object_info, ground_truth_topic: /v2x/rsu1/lidar1/object_info_groundtruth}

To add a sensor, add an entry. To remove one, delete it or set enabled: false. Line-of-sight checks use exactly the sensors of this file.

docs.title: Object-info publishers (CooL4 DM)
docs.text:
object_info_publishers:
- name: all_rsus
  rsus: [all]                        # RSU names, or all
  topic: /v2x/object_info
  ground_truth_topic: /v2x/object_info_groundtruth
  hz: 10
  noise: {position: Default, rotation: Default, dimension: Default, probability: Default}
  network: [DSRC, Cellular]          # adds /v2x/object_info/DSRC and /v2x/object_info/Cellular

per_sensor_object_info:              # rate and noise of the per-sensor topics
  hz: 10
  noise: {position: Default, rotation: Default, dimension: Default, probability: Default}

A publisher merges what the sensors of its RSUs see. An object seen by several sensors is sent once and lists every sensor in information_source_list. For the message content and the ID layout, see Object Info.

docs.title: Autoware object and traffic-signal publishers
docs.text:
autoware_object_publishers:          # autoware_auto_perception_msgs/PredictedObjects
- name: rsu1
  rsus: [Ganken]
  topic: /v2x/rsu1/predicted_object
  station_id: 1
  hz: 10
  noise: {position: Default, rotation: Default, dimension: Default, probability: Default}
  network: [DSRC, Cellular]

traffic_signal_publishers:           # v2x_msgs/V2XSignals
- name: rsu1
  station_id: 1
  intersections: [Ganken]            # TrafficIntersection names in the scene
  topics: [/v2x/rsu1/traffic_signals, /v2x/traffic_signals]
  hz: 10
  signal_id: relation                # relation = Lanelet2 regulatory-element IDs, way = traffic-light way IDs

docs.title: Sensor Types
docs.text:
File config/defaults/sensor_types.yaml Web viewer Settings → Defaults Unity export V2X → Config → Export Scene To Config

These defaults are shared by all scenarios.

pseudo_sensor_types:
- name: lidar_60x22deg_60m
  kind: lidar            # lidar | camera
  h_fov_deg: 60
  v_fov_deg: 22
  range_m: 60

An RSU sensor refers to a type by name and may override h_fov_deg, v_fov_deg and range_m. raw_sensor_types lists the LiDAR and camera prefabs that raw_sensors.yaml can create.

docs.title: Signal Timing
docs.text:
File config/scenarios/<name>/signals.yaml Web viewer Settings → Signals Unity export V2X → Config → Export Simulation And Signal Timing To Config 
intersections:
- name: Kakeiken              # TrafficIntersection object (see Kashiwa Scene Names)
  enabled: true               # false = keep the scene timing
  steps:
  - duration_s: 35
    lights: V1 green, V2 red, V3 green, P1 red, P2 green
  - duration_s: 3
    lights: P2 green flashing
  # … one entry per step, in order; the cycle repeats

Each intersection runs its lighting steps in order and repeats them. duration_s sets how long each step lasts. lights describes what the step shows (V1 = vehicle group 1, P1 = pedestrian group 1); it is written by the exporter and not read. The number of steps and what they show come from the scene, so steps cannot be added or removed here. Signal info (remaining time) and the V2X signal topics follow the new timing.

docs.title: Simulation
docs.text:
File config/scenarios/<name>/simulation.yaml Web viewer Settings → Simulation Unity export V2X → Config → Export Simulation And Signal Timing To Config 
time_scale: 1                 # simulation speed, 1 = real time (> 0, at most 100)
seed: 0                       # one seed for everything random; leave empty for a different run every time
ego:
  vehicle: BusAutowareFinal   # an ego vehicle of the scene (tag Ego): BusAutowareFinal, Lexus RX450h 2015 Sample Sensor
  pose: {x: 4769.09, y: 73083.82, z: 18.38, heading_deg: 241}   # start pose; omit to keep the scene pose
lighting:
  time_of_day: '17:30'        # local time; empty = the sun of the scene
  date: '2025-06-21'
  latitude_deg: 35.9
  longitude_deg: 139.94
  utc_offset_h: 9
  # sun_elevation_deg: 40     # or place the sun directly (both values)
  # sun_azimuth_deg: 180
  sun_intensity_lux: 100000
  color_temperature_k: 6570
  night_intensity_lux: 0.5    # moonlight when the sun is below the horizon
weather:
  fog_visibility_m: 0         # e.g. 150 for thick fog; 0 = no fog
  fog_height_m: 60
loggers:
  output_dir: SimulationOutput
  npc_area:                   # NPC vehicles and pedestrians inside the log area (LogArea)
    enabled: true
    cars_csv: Scenario_car.csv
    humans_csv: Scenario_human.csv
    every_n_frames: 2         # 0 = every interval_s instead
    interval_s: 0.05
  ego:                        # state of the ego vehicle (LogAutonomous)
    enabled: false
    csv: Autonomous.csv
    spawn_validation_csv: AutonomousSpawnValidation.csv
    prefix: Auto
    interval_s: 0.005
  • Ego vehicle. The chosen vehicle is switched on and the other ego vehicles are switched off. The traffic manager, the ScenarioSelector teleport keys and the Selected Car dropdown follow it. Its raw sensors are set up from raw_sensors.yaml before it starts.
  • Seed. It seeds Unity's random numbers, the traffic manager (it replaces the seed of vehicles.yaml), line-of-sight UUIDs and the object numbers of object info. Physics and frame timing still differ a little between runs, so runs are similar but not bit-identical.
  • Sun. time_of_day places the sun from the date and the position (NOAA formulas). When the sun is below the horizon, a dim light opposite it (night_intensity_lux) keeps the scene readable. The camera exposure of the scene is automatic.
  • Fog. It adds an HDRP fog to the scene's global volume. Visibility is the distance where objects fade out (mean free path × 3). It affects cameras, not the pseudo sensors or the RGL LiDARs.
  • Loggers. Files are written to output_dir (relative to the project folder, or the build folder) as <name>_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.csv. See Loggers.
  • Time scale. It is also passed to the ROS clock, so /clock and the timestamps follow it.

docs.title: Teleports
docs.text:
File config/scenarios/<name>/teleports.yaml Web viewer Settings → Teleports Unity export V2X → Config → Export Pedestrians And Teleports To Config

A teleport gate moves the ego vehicle when it drives into the trigger box.

teleports:
- name: First gate
  enabled: true
  trigger: {x: 4431.903, y: 73109.227, z: 19.707, heading_deg: 70.4}
  trigger_size: {x: 5.11, y: 2, z: 6.92}      # width, height, length (m)
  strategy: lane_midpoint                     # lane_midpoint | random_point
  clearance_radius_m: 15                      # NPCs this close to the target are removed
  delay_s: 0
  random_delay_s: [0, 0]
  lane_midpoint:
    lanelets: [1034, 1118, 1113, 1104, 1086, 1093, 1082, 1071]   # candidate lanes
    midpoint_lanelet: 328
    midpoint_fraction: 0.5
    cruise_speed_kmh: 30
    acceleration_mps2: 2
    arrival_window_s: [0, 90]
    spacing_m: 10
    include_endpoints: true
  # random_point: random_points: [{x: …, y: …, z: …, heading_deg: …}]
Field Meaning trigger, trigger_size Box the ego drives into: centre and heading in the map frame; size x = width, y = height, z = length (m) strategy lane_midpoint: pick a start point on the listed lanes (below). random_point: one of random_points, chosen at random. clearance_radius_m NPC vehicles closer than this to the target are removed before the ego arrives delay_s, random_delay_s Wait before the jump: delay_s plus a random value in [min, max] lane_midpoint.lanelets Lanes the ego may be placed on; candidate points every spacing_m along them (include_endpoints: also the lane ends) lane_midpoint.midpoint_lanelet, midpoint_fraction Reference point the ego should reach: this far along that lane (0 = start, 1 = end) lane_midpoint.arrival_window_s A target time is drawn at random in [min, max]. The candidate whose estimated driving time to the reference point is closest wins. lane_midpoint.cruise_speed_kmh, acceleration_mps2 Used for that estimate: accelerate from 0 to cruise speed, then drive on

In the web viewer, Pick target lanes on map toggles lanes in lanelets.

docs.title: Vehicle Traffic
docs.text:
File config/scenarios/<name>/vehicles.yaml Web viewer Settings → Vehicles Unity export V2X → Config → Export Vehicle Traffic To Config 
lanes_root: AutowareSimulator/Enviroment /TrafficLanes
template_traffic_manager: ScenarioSelector/Cool4 Kakeiken Overal Evaluation /New NPC - Kashiwa High
seed: 0
max_vehicles: 200
spawn_distance_to_ego_m: 30          # no spawning closer than this to the ego vehicle
spawn_clearance_m: 4                 # free space needed around the spawn point
maximum_spawns: 4000                 # 0 = unlimited
behaviour:
  deadlock_timeout_s: 8              # standing while yielding this long -> takes the right of way
  forced_pass_s: 6                   # ... for this long
  forced_pass_radius_m: 70
  stuck_despawn_s: 180               # standing still this long for any reason -> removed (0 = never)
  standstill_speed_mps: 0.3
vehicle_types:
- {prefab: Hatchback Variant, weight: 1}
- {prefab: SmallCar Variant, weight: 1}
- {prefab: Taxi Variant, weight: 1}
- {prefab: Van Variant, weight: 1}
spawn_points:
- name: lanelet779
  lanelet: 779
  vehicles_per_minute: 5.15          # ± 25 % random spacing
  position: {x: 4352.18, y: 73301.3, z: 18.62}
branches:                            # where a lane splits
- from_lanelet: 1034
  to:
  - {lanelet: 1088, ratio: 0.33}
  - {lanelet: 1089, ratio: 0.67}     # normalised; next lanes that are not listed get 0
  • Lanelet numbers are the names of the simulator's traffic lanes (lanelet<number> under lanes_root). In the web viewer, click a lane in Settings → Vehicles to see its number and next lanes and to add a spawn point or branch ratios.
  • One traffic manager runs the traffic. The template_traffic_manager of the scene supplies the ego vehicle, layers and vehicle dynamics, and the scene's other traffic managers are switched off. vehicle_types may use any NPC prefab that a traffic manager of the scene knows.
  • A vehicle is created only when the spawn point is clear. The next one is scheduled from vehicles_per_minute.
  • behaviour.forced_pass_radius_m: at most one vehicle within this distance gets the right of way at a time (the one that has waited longest), so two blocked vehicles at the same intersection do not both go. behaviour.standstill_speed_mps: below this speed a vehicle counts as standing.
  • Right of way: vehicles follow the lane rules of the scene. If a vehicle has waited to yield for deadlock_timeout_s while the others also wait, it gets the right of way. Vehicles that have not moved for stuck_despawn_s are removed. Vehicles also leave at the end of their route.

docs.title: DM Protocols
docs.text:
The V2X E2E Simulator can publish what its roadside units (RSUs) see, and what its traffic signals show, in the Dynamic Map (DM) data formats. That lets it stand in for a real roadside infrastructure and feed a DM data-linkage platform, or any node that consumes DM messages, without building an adapter.

This section explains those formats and how the simulator produces them.

Protocol family What it covers Pages CooL4 DM The CooL4 data-linkage platform API (CooL4 データ連携 PF API 仕様, v0.8.1). Object information (物標情報) and signal information (信号情報) published as ROS 2 messages from the dm_*_msgs packages. Overview, Object Info, Signal Info, Topic List

docs.title: How DM output fits into the simulator
docs.text:
The simulator already publishes Autoware-compatible topics (PredictedObjects, TrafficSignalArray, …) and the project's own v2x_msgs (V2XSignals). The DM topics are published alongside them from the same ground truth, so the same scene can drive Autoware and a DM platform at once. Network effects (delay, packet loss) are also generated by the simulator itself, see Delayed copies.

                         ┌──────────────── Unity scene ────────────────┐
  NPC vehicles,          │  Pseudo sensors ──► ObjectInfo ─────────────┼──► dm_object_info_msgs/ObjectInfoArray
  pedestrians,           │  (MockSensor)                               │     /v2x/object_info[_groundtruth]
  cyclists               │                                             │
                         │  TrafficIntersection ──► DMSignalInfo-      │
  Traffic lights ───────►│  (lighting sequences)    Publisher ─────────┼──► dm_signal_info_msgs/SignalInfoArray
                         │                                             │     /signal_info
                         │  (unchanged) PredictedObjects, V2XSignals, …┼──► Autoware / V2X topics
                         └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Getting the message packages
docs.text:
A subscriber needs the DM message definitions. They are published together with the other simulator messages:

  • Repository: github.com/tlab-wide/v2x_e2e_msgs
  • DM packages: dm_object_info_msgs, dm_signal_info_msgs, dm_freespace_info_msgs, dm_sensor_info_msgs, dm_debug_msgs (under src/dm_msgs/)
mkdir -p ~/v2x_ws/src && cd ~/v2x_ws/src
git clone https://github.com/tlab-wide/v2x_e2e_msgs.git
cd ~/v2x_ws
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
colcon build
source install/setup.bash

The simulator itself needs no build step. The C# bindings (dm_*_msgs_assembly.dll and their native libraries) are already in Assets/Ros2ForUnity/Plugins/.

docs.title: Quick check
docs.text:
With the simulator running, and from a terminal where the workspace above is sourced:

ros2 topic list | grep -E "signal_info|object_info"
ros2 topic echo /signal_info --once
ros2 topic hz /signal_info

ROS domain and DDS

The DM topics use the same ROS 2 node as all other simulator topics, so the usual ROS_DOMAIN_ID / RMW_IMPLEMENTATION settings apply. See Troubleshooting if no topics show up.

docs.title: CooL4 DM Protocols
docs.text:
CooL4 (自動運転レベル４等先進モビリティサービス研究開発・社会実装プロジェクト テーマ 4) defines a data-linkage platform (データ連携 PF). It collects dynamic information from vehicles and roadside equipment and hands it to automated-driving systems. Its API specification, CooL4 データ連携 PF API 仕様 v0.8.1, defines four kinds of dynamic information:

Information Japanese Purpose In the simulator Object information 物標情報 Position and state of vehicles, pedestrians, … Published: Object Info Signal information 信号情報 Current colour of each traffic signal and when it changes Published: Signal Info Free-space information フリースペース情報 Areas known to be free of objects Message package included; not covered here Sensor information センサー情報 Sensor mounting position and detection area Message package included; not covered here

The ROS 2 packages dm_object_info_msgs, dm_signal_info_msgs, … are a direct transcription of the spec's logical data formats. Each data element (DE) or data frame (DF) of the spec becomes a small message with a value field and named constants.

docs.title: How the simulator plays the roles of the platform
docs.text:
Real deployment                               Simulator
 ───────────────                               ─────────
 Roadside sensors (LiDAR, cameras)        ≙    Pseudo sensors (MockSensor) on RSU poles
 Cooperative roadside unit (協調型路側機)   ≙    ObjectInfo component, one per RSU / sensor
 Traffic signal controller                ≙    TrafficIntersection lighting sequences
 DM messenger / ROS2DMI                   ≙    DMSignalInfoPublisher (/signal_info)

Every DM message the simulator sends is built from the simulation's ground truth. Object positions, sizes and speeds can be perturbed with the noise settings to mimic sensor error. Messages can also be delayed or dropped with the built-in network model (see Delayed copies).

docs.title: Conventions shared by all CooL4 messages
Units
docs.text:
The spec fixes a small set of units (§3.2, §5). The simulator converts from Unity (metres, degrees, seconds) as follows:

Quantity DM unit Conversion in the simulator Unknown value Length / size 0.01 m metres × 100 65535 (ObjectDimensionValue) Azimuth (heading, direction) 0.0125° clockwise from north degrees × 80 28800 Speed 0.01 m/s m/s × 100 16383 Latitude / longitude 0.1 µdeg (1e-7 deg) deg × 10 000 000 900000001 / 1800000001 Altitude 0.01 m metres × 100 800001 Remaining signal time 0.1 s seconds × 10 65535

docs.title: Timestamp (DE_TimestampIts)
docs.text:
TimestampIts.value is the number of milliseconds since 2004‑01‑01 00:00. The spec counts from UTC. The simulator subtracts 1072882800000 from the current Unix time in milliseconds, which is 2004‑01‑01 00:00 JST. As a result, simulator timestamps run 9 hours (32 400 000 ms) ahead of a strict UTC reading.

All DM publishers in the simulator (object info and signal info) use the same helper, ObjectInfo.GetITSTimeInMilliseconds(), so timestamps are consistent with each other.

Converting to UTC

To recover UTC Unix time from a simulator timestamp, add 1072882800000, not 1072915200000. If the DM side assumes the spec's UTC epoch, account for the 9 h offset.

docs.title: Unknown values and optional fields
docs.text: The spec makes most fields optional, and every optional field has an "unknown" value. Fields the simulator does not fill keep the default from the .msg file, which is the unknown value where one is defined. For example, MinTimeToChange.value defaults to 65535 and AzimuthValue.value defaults to 28800.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text: Identifier Size Used in Defined in Object ID (物標 ID) 64 bit ObjectInfo.id, information_source_list spec §3.3.3, see Object Info CRP ID (交差点 ID) 32 bit SignalInfo.crp_id assigned by the traffic administrator Signal ID (信号灯器 ID) 8 bit SignalInfo.signal_id_list spec §3.6.3, see Signal Info

docs.title: Delayed copies (network model)
docs.text:
Each DM publisher can also publish delayed and lossy copies of its messages. The general profiles live on the NetworkSimulator component (the Noise and Delay Profile object in the scene), and each publisher can add its own. Each profile appends a suffix to the topic name:

Suffix Delay Packet loss /DSRC 100 ms 5 % /Cellular 400 ms 0 %

For example, /v2x/object_info is also published as /v2x/object_info/DSRC and /v2x/object_info/Cellular, and /signal_info as /signal_info/DSRC and /signal_info/Cellular. Turn this on or off per component with Enable Delayed Messages.

  • Signal Info: how traffic lights become SignalInfoArray messages, including remaining time and the Kashiwa signal ID table.
  • Topic List: every DM topic in the Kashiwa scene, with type, rate and QoS.

docs.title: Object Info (物標情報)
docs.text: Object information describes the position and state of objects on and around the road: vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists (spec §3.3). In the simulator, roadside pseudo sensors detect these objects. The ObjectInfo component then publishes them as recognised object information (認識物標情報), the way a cooperative roadside unit (協調型路側機) would.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
NPC vehicles / pedestrians / cyclists          (ground truth in Unity)
          │
          ▼
 Pseudo sensors (MockSensor: LiDAR / camera FOV + line-of-sight checks), each with a sensor ID
          │  GetSeenObjects()
          ▼
 ObjectInfo component                                            every 1 / Hz s
          │  1. collect every object seen by its sensors, by the sensors of its Sources (other
          │     ObjectInfo components) and of its Rsu Sensors groups, each with its RSU ID; ego excluded
          │  2. build one ObjectInfo per object, twice:
          │       with noise    → topic              e.g. /v2x/object_info
          │       ground truth  → topicGroundTruth   e.g. /v2x/object_info_groundtruth
          │  3. optional delayed / lossy copies of the noisy topic (/DSRC, /Cellular)
          ▼
 dm_object_info_msgs/ObjectInfoArray

An object seen by several sensors is sent once, with every sensor that saw it in information_source_list. The ground truth contains the same objects with the same IDs, without position, rotation, size or existence noise.

docs.title: Message format
docs.text:
dm_object_info_msgs/ObjectInfoArray holds ObjectInfo[] array. The table lists every field the simulator fills; all other fields keep their "unknown" default (see conventions).

Field Spec item Value published by the simulator id.value 物標 ID [required] Same as information_source_list[0] (see Object ID layout) time.value 情報取得時刻 [required] Last update time of the sensor of information_source_list[0], as DE_TimestampIts (epoch note) object_class[0].id.value 物標種別 1 VEHICLE if the object is an NPCVehicle, else 2 PERSON (pedestrians and cyclists) object_class[0].confidence.value 分類信頼度 101 existency.value 存在信頼度 Ground truth: 101 (certain). docs.title: Object ID layout
docs.text:
Spec §3.3.3 packs every object ID into 64 bits. The top two bits say who assigned it:

 bits 63-62  meaning                                       remaining 62 bits
 00          cooperative roadside unit itself              reserved (30) | device ID (32)
 01          object's own pseudonym ID (自己物標)            reserved (12) | pseudonym ID (50)
 10          object recognised by a roadside unit           number assigned by the RSU (30) | device ID (32)
 11          object recognised by a vehicle                 number assigned by the vehicle (12) | pseudonym ID (50)

The simulator plays roadside units, so it always uses 10. It splits the 30-bit "number assigned by the RSU" into a sensor ID and an object number:

  63 62 61 ......... 56 55 ....... 48 47 ........... 32 31 ............................ 0
 ┌─────┬──────────────┬─────────────┬─────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┐
 │ 1 0 │  0 (6 bit)   │ sensor ID   │ object number   │ RSU / device ID (rsuId)        │
 │     │              │  (8 bit)    │  (16 bit)       │  e.g. 0x12020002               │
 └─────┴──────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘
  • RSU ID: the Rsu Id field of the component the sensor belongs to, a hex string such as 0x12020002. A combined publisher keeps each source's RSU ID.
  • Sensor ID: the Sensor Id of the MockSensor that saw the object.
  • Object number: a random number (1–65 535) drawn once per object (keyed by the object's UUID) from one table shared by all ObjectInfo components. So the same object has the same number on every topic and at every intersection, and a number is never given to two objects (the table starts over after 65 535 objects).

information_source_list holds one such ID per sensor that saw the object, sorted by RSU ID and then sensor ID. id copies the first one. It changes only when the set of sensors that see the object changes so that a different sensor comes first.

Differences from the spec

  • The spec expects information_source_list to contain the observing device's ID (00 + device ID). The simulator puts the per-sensor recognised-object IDs there instead, which lets a consumer tell which sensors saw the object.
  • The list is not capped at 4 entries.

docs.title: Publishing rate
docs.text:
The Hz field is the publishing rate: ObjectInfo.Update() publishes every 1 / Hz seconds of simulation time, carrying the remainder over so the average stays at Hz even when the frame rate does not divide it. All publishers of the Kashiwa scene use 10 Hz. Verify with ros2 topic hz.

QoS: best effort, volatile, keep-last 1.

docs.title: Reading the Messages
docs.text: This page shows how to look at the CooL4 DM topics while the simulator runs, and how to read the content: the units, the light codes, and how object and signal IDs are built. The field-by-field specification is on the Object Info and Signal Info pages.

docs.title: Three ways to look at the topics
docs.text:
All three need ROS 2 Humble and the built v2x_e2e_msgs workspace sourced, with the same middleware as the simulator:

source ~/v2x_e2e_msgs/install/setup.bash

docs.title: Object IDs
docs.text:
Every object ID is 64 bits. The simulator acts as a roadside unit, so the top two bits are always 10 (object recognised by a roadside unit, spec §3.3.3):

Bits 63–62 61–56 55–48 47–32 31–0 Field owner reserved sensor ID object number RSU ID 0x8003a9ac12020002 10 000000 0x03 = 3 0xa9ac = 43436 0x12020002 = Kakeiken_A 0x8004a9ac12020003 10 000000 0x04 = 4 0xa9ac = 43436 0x12020003 = Kakeiken_B
  • Object number: one random number per object (1–65 535). It is the same on every topic and in every intersection while the object exists. It is the part to use to track an object.
  • Sensor ID + RSU ID: which sensor saw it. A different sensor gives a different ID for the same object.
  • information_source_list holds one ID per sensor that sees the object, sorted by RSU ID, then sensor ID. id is the first of them.

To split an ID in Python:

def split_object_id(value):
    return {
        'owner':         value >> 62,               # 2 = recognised by RSU
        'sensor_id':     (value >> 48) & 0xFF,
        'object_number': (value >> 32) & 0xFFFF,
        'rsu_id':        value & 0xFFFFFFFF,
    }

split_object_id(9224403018286497794)
# {'owner': 2, 'sensor_id': 3, 'object_number': 43436, 'rsu_id': 302120962}   (302120962 = 0x12020002)

docs.text:
A signal ID is one byte: which approach (方路, 1–8) the traffic comes from and where it goes.

docs.title: Light codes and times
docs.text:
main_light Vehicle signal Pedestrian signal 1 dark dark 2 red flashing red flashing 3 red red 5 green green 7 yellow green flashing (青点滅) 9 yellow flashing yellow flashing
  • min_time_to_change / max_time_to_change are in 0.1 s. They are equal because the signals run on a fixed cycle.
  • Entry [0] gives the time left for the current light. The following entries give how long each next light lasts.
  • arrow_light is a bit field: 0x40 left, 0x10 straight, 0x04 right. The Kashiwa signals have no arrows, so it is 0.
