docs.title: Signal Info (信号情報)
docs.text:
The simulator publishes the state of its traffic signals in the CooL4 signal-information format (dm_signal_info_msgs, spec §3.6). For every configured intersection it publishes:

  • which logical signals (信号灯器) are being described: the CRP ID and signal ID list
  • the colour they show now: main light and green arrows
  • how long that colour remains, plus the upcoming colours and their durations

All five signalised intersections on the Kashiwa-no-ha bus route are published continuously, wherever the ego vehicle is. DM receives the same stream a roadside DM messenger would send, so the old signal_info_converter_node (/v2x/traffic_signals → /signal_info) is no longer needed.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
TrafficIntersection (one per intersection, in the Kashiwa environment prefab)
 │  lightingSequences: [ {intervalSec, group → bulbs}, ... ]  (looped)
 │  remembers: current sequence index, the time it started, current bulbs of every group
 │
 │  TryGetGroupTimeline(group)  ──►  [ (bulbs now, time left in this step),
 │                                     (bulbs in next step, step length), ... one full cycle ]
 ▼
 DMSignalInfoPublisher  (every 1/Hz s)
 │  for each intersection → for each configured signal group:
 │     1. bulbs → MainLightIndication + ArrowLightIndication
 │     2. merge consecutive steps with the same light → remaining time of each light
 │     3. build SignalInfo { crp_id, signal_id_list, time, …, signal_light_info_list }
 ▼
 /signal_info                       SignalInfoArray, all intersections   (consumed by DM)
 /signal_info/DSRC, /…/Cellular     delayed / lossy copies (network model)

The light state comes straight from the lighting sequence that drives the Unity traffic lights. The colour the DM consumer receives is therefore always the colour shown in the scene and obeyed by the NPC vehicles.

Why not read the TrafficLight objects?

A TrafficLight only knows its current bulbs. The remaining time (残秒数) exists only in the intersection's lighting sequence. Pedestrian phases (groups 10–13) exist only in the sequence too: at these intersections they have no visible lights. Reading the sequence gives both.

docs.title: Message format
docs.text:
dm_signal_info_msgs/SignalInfoArray
└─ SignalInfo[] array
   ├─ dm_object_info_msgs/CrpId        crp_id                 交差点 ID (uint32)
   ├─ SignalId[]                       signal_id_list         信号灯器 ID list (uint8 each, 1–8)
   ├─ dm_object_info_msgs/TimestampIts time                   情報生成時刻 (ms)
   ├─ SignalState                      state                  信号状態情報
   ├─ SpecificControlFlags             specific_control_flags 特定制御動作中フラグ
   ├─ EventCount                       event_count            イベントカウンタ
   ├─ CountDownStopFlag                count_down_stop_flag   カウントダウン停止フラグ (OFF=0, ON=1)
   └─ SignalLightInfo[]                signal_light_info_list 灯色出力情報 (1–12), [0] = now
      ├─ MainLightIndication   main_light          主灯色表示
      ├─ ArrowLightIndication  arrow_light         青矢信号表示 (bit field)
      ├─ MinTimeToChange       min_time_to_change  最小残秒数 (0.1 s)
      └─ MaxTimeToChange       max_time_to_change  最大残秒数 (0.1 s)

docs.title: Field mapping
docs.text:
Field Value published by the simulator crp_id.value CRP ID of the intersection (see Kashiwa signal IDs) signal_id_list[] Signal IDs of one signal group. Padded with 0 (SignalId.UNKNOWN) to 8 elements, like the DM messenger (ROS2DMI) output. Turn Pad Signal Id List off to send only the real IDs. More than 8 IDs are split into several SignalInfo (spec §3.6.2). time.value Generation time, DE_TimestampIts (see timestamp note) state.value 0. Under consideration in the spec (SIP-adus). specific_control_flags.value 0. Under consideration in the spec. event_count.value 0. The fixed-time signals never change in a way that time alone cannot predict. count_down_stop_flag.value OFF (0) while the remaining time counts down. ON (1) when the light never changes in the cycle. The remaining time is then unknown and does not count down. signal_light_info_list[0] Current light. min/max_time_to_change = time until it changes. signal_light_info_list[1..] Following lights in order. min/max_time_to_change = how long each is shown.

Because the simulated signals are fixed-time, the remaining times are exact, so min_time_to_change == max_time_to_change (spec: "残秒数が確定している場合には，最小残秒数と最大残秒数に同じ値を格納する").

docs.title: Light colour (main_light)
docs.text:
Bulb shown in Unity Vehicle signal Pedestrian signal no bulb lit 1 DARK 1 DARK red, solid 3 RED_LIGHT 3 RED_LIGHT red, flashing 2 FLASHING_RED 2 FLASHING_RED green, solid 5 PERMISSIVE_GREEN 5 PERMISSIVE_GREEN green, flashing 5 PERMISSIVE_GREEN 7 (青点滅, flashing green) yellow, solid 7 PERMISSIVE_YELLOW 7 (青点滅, flashing green) yellow, flashing 9 FLASHING_YELLOW 9 FLASHING_YELLOW

Value 7 means yellow for vehicle signals and flashing green for pedestrian signals (spec §5, DE_MainLightIndication). Values 4, 6 and 8 are never used.

docs.title: Green arrows (arrow_light)
docs.text: Bit field of DE_青矢信号表示方向: bit 6 left, bit 4 straight, bit 2 right. A lit LEFT_ARROW_BULB, UP_ARROW_BULB or RIGHT_ARROW_BULB sets the matching bit. The Kashiwa signals have no arrow bulbs, so arrow_light is always 0 there.

docs.title: Remaining time (残秒数)
docs.text:
TrafficIntersection records which lighting step is active and when it started. For a signal group the publisher:

  1. takes the group's bulbs for the current step and the next steps of one full cycle. A step that does not mention the group keeps its previous bulbs.
  2. converts each step to a main_light / arrow_light pair, and merges consecutive steps with the same light.
  3. publishes the first merged entry with the time left: the rest of the current step plus the following steps with the same light. The next entries carry their full durations.
  4. drops the last entry if it shows the current light again, because the look-ahead window cuts it short. It caps the list at 12 entries (spec maximum).
  5. if the light never changes during the cycle, publishes a single entry with min/max_time_to_change = 65535 (UNKNOWN) and count_down_stop_flag = ON.

Worked example. がん研 (Ganken), 方路1 (group 0), 10 s after the cycle starts, with the environment prefab's sequence (the Kashiwa scene overrides it, so live values differ): G 50 s → Y 3 s → R (7+3+3+30+3+3 s) → G …

signal_light_info_list main_light min/max_time_to_change Meaning [0] 5 (green) 400 green for another 40.0 s [1] 7 (yellow) 30 then yellow for 3.0 s [2] 3 (red) 490 then red for 49.0 s

The remaining time is measured in simulation time (Time.time). It slows down and speeds up with the simulation time scale, exactly like the lights themselves.

docs.title: Signal ID layout
docs.text:
A signal ID identifies a logical signal: the go/stop indication for one inbound lane to one outbound lane, not a physical signal head (spec §3.6.3). It is built from the approach IDs (方路 ID, 1–8) of the intersection:

 vehicle signal     [ inbound approach (4 bit) | outbound approach (4 bit) ]   e.g. 0x12 = from 方路1 to 方路2
 pedestrian signal  [ crossed approach (4 bit) | 0000                     ]   e.g. 0x30 = crossing 方路3
 0x00 = unknown, 0xFF = always allowed

Signal IDs that always show the same state are sent together in one signal_id_list. All movements from one approach therefore share one SignalInfo, for example [0x11, 0x12, 0x13] for everything entering from 方路1.

docs.title: Kashiwa signal IDs
docs.text:
The IDs below follow 東大_柏の葉実験環境について_信号情報について抜粋, the signal ID sheet of the Kashiwa-no-ha experiment environment. Approach directions are given north-up. Entries marked sheet match the DM messenger output in the sheet, including the order inside the list. Entries marked spec are not in the sheet; they are built with the §3.6.3 rule so that every approach and crossing is covered.

docs.title: How the intersections were matched
docs.text:
The Unity intersections were matched to the sheet in two steps (before v3.1.1 their GameObjects were called crossroad1 … crossroad 14; they now carry the names below):

  1. Each intersection's traffic-light Lanelet2 IDs (TrafficLightLaneletID) were placed on the Kashiwa Lanelet2 map. From south-east to north-west: 駅前 Ekimae (35.8945, 139.9498) → 若柴 Wakashiba (35.8979, 139.9495) → 科警研 Kakeiken (35.8960, 139.9418) → がん研 Ganken (35.9007, 139.9390) → 東大前 Todaimae (35.9001, 139.9376).
  2. The legs were numbered with the bus turns given in the sheet. For example, at 駅前 the 駅→東大 bus turns right from 方路1 towards 若柴 in the north, so 方路1 is the east leg.

The resulting leg layout matches every diagram in the sheet. It also matches the pedestrian groupings the sheet gives for がん研, 科警研 and 駅前.

docs.title: Using it in a scene
docs.text:
The publisher is a single component, DMSignalInfoPublisher (Assets/V2X/Script/CustomMsg/DMSignalInfoPublisher.cs). It is shipped ready-configured as a prefab:

  1. Drag Assets/V2X/Prefabs/DM/DM Signal Info Publisher.prefab into the scene, for example under RSUs/Publishers.
  2. Save the scene and press Play. /signal_info appears right away.

It does not depend on an RSU GameObject being active. The intersections are found by GameObject name when play starts, so it works with the RSU objects disabled.

1. Find the intersection's TrafficIntersection and note its GameObject name and the group numbers in its Traffic Light Groups / Lighting Sequences.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Fixed-time signals. min_time_to_change always equals max_time_to_change. event_count, state and specific_control_flags are always 0.
  • Groups that never change. A group that the lighting sequence sets only once per cycle (for example a pedestrian group) never changes; it is published with an UNKNOWN remaining time and count_down_stop_flag = ON.
  • Scene overrides. The Kashiwa scene overrides the lighting sequences and light groups of がん研, 科警研, 若柴 and 駅前 on top of the environment prefab, and 科警研's GameObject carries a second, disabled TrafficIntersection. The publisher uses the enabled component, and the approach-to-group table above matches the scene. If you change the light groups in the scene, update the publisher's signal groups too; a group that is never lit is logged once as a warning and not published.
  • Lighting sequence of 東大前. In Todaimae (not overridden by the scene) one step sets group 0 twice (g0=R g0=G g2=R). Group 1 (東大前 方路3) therefore goes red → yellow without ever turning green. The DM output faithfully reports what the scene shows.
  • Timestamp epoch. The epoch is JST-based, consistent with object info (see timestamp note).

docs.title: Localhost settings
docs.text:
The simulation relies on specific network configurations to ensure seamless communication between the V2X_E2E_Simulator and Autoware. To set up the necessary localhost environment, add the following lines to your ~/.bashrc file:

if [ ! -e /tmp/cycloneDDS_configured ]; then
    sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=2147483647
    sudo ip link set lo multicast on
    touch /tmp/cycloneDDS_configured
fi

and these lines to ~/.profile or in either of files: ~/.bash_profile or ~/.bash_login:

export ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp

Warning

A system restart is required for these changes to work.

docs.title: Controlling Features
docs.text: Without using Autoware, you can manually control the cars to create your desired scenario.

docs.title: Vehicle selection
docs.text:
• Choose the ego vehicle (Bus or Lexus) from the vehicle dropdown in the UI.
  • The selected vehicle is activated and the other one is deactivated. The Bus is active when the simulator starts.
  • Keyboard driving, teleport and the speed/gear display always apply to the currently active vehicle.

docs.title: 1. Basic Controls (gear)
docs.text:
• D (Drive) → Press to enable driving mode.
  • P (Park) → Press to stop the vehicle.
  • R (Reverse) → Press to drive in reverse mode.
  • N (Neutral) → Press to shift to neutral.

docs.title: 2. Driving Controls
docs.text:
• After pressing D (Drive), use the arrow keys to move around the city (Up = accelerate, Down = brake, Left/Right = steer).
  • Turn signals: 1 = left, 2 = right, 3 = hazard, 4 = off (main keyboard number keys).
  • When the vehicle is driven by Autoware, pressing an arrow key takes over control (the control mode switches to manual). The gear you select with the keyboard is kept; it is not reset to the vehicle's previous gear.

docs.title: 3. Teleport Feature
docs.text:
• There are four predefined start points in the scene.
  • Use the following keys to teleport the currently active vehicle (Bus or Lexus):
  • Q, E, F, X → Teleport to start points 1, 2, 3 and 4.
  • Before moving the vehicle, NPC vehicles near the destination are removed (within clearanceRadius, 15 m in the scene) and the teleport waits teleportDelay (1 s in the scene).

docs.title: 4. Manual Object Creation
docs.text:
• Use button O to spawn objects in scenarios where this feature is available (SpawnerOnWaypoint).

Figure: Defualt keys for extra functionalities

Info

It is advised to checkout the Quick Start Demo tutorial before reading this section.

This page is a tutorial for setting up V2X_E2E Simulator in Unity project.

docs.title: System setup (Ubuntu 22)
docs.text:
1. Make sure your machine meets the required hardware specifications.

    • NOTE: PC requirements may vary depending on simulation contents which may change as the simulator develops

  2. Prepare a desktop PC with Ubuntu 22.04 installed.

  3. Install Nvidia drivers and Vulkan Graphics API.

  4. Install git.

  5. Set the ROS 2 middleware and the localhost only mode in ~/.profile (or, in ~/.bash_profile or ~/bash_login if either of those exists) file:

    export ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp

    Warning

    A system restart is required for these changes to work.

  6. Set the system optimizations by adding this code to the very bottom of your ~/.bashrc file:

    if [ ! -e /tmp/cycloneDDS_configured ]; then
    sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=2147483647
    sudo ip link set lo multicast on
    touch /tmp/cycloneDDS_configured
fi

    Info

    As a result, each time you run the terminal (bash prompt), your OS will be configured for the best ROS 2 performance. Make sure you open your terminal at least once before running any instance of the V2X_E2E Simulator (or the Editor running the V2X_E2E Simulator).

  7. install nvidia driver, The easiest way to be sure about your version is by using 'Software & Updates' in Ubuntu.

    Warning

    Currently, there are cases where the Nvidia driver version is incomptable, resulting in Segmentation fault. In that case, please use the tested Nvidia driver version in our case is 580.

docs.title: ROS 2
docs.text:
V2X_E2E Simulator comes with a standalone flavor of Ros2ForUnity. This means that, to avoid internal conflicts between different ROS 2 versions, you shouldn't run the Editor or V2X_E2E Simulator binary with ROS 2 sourced.

Warning

Do not run the V2X_E2E Simulator, Unity Hub, or the Editor with ROS 2 sourced.

  • Make sure that the terminal which you are using to run Unity Hub, Editor, or V2X doesn't have ROS 2 sourced.
  • It is common to have ROS 2 sourced automatically with ~/.bashrc or ~/.profile. Make sure it is not obscuring your working environment:
    • Running Unity Hub from the Ubuntu GUI menu takes the environment configuration from ~/.profile.
    • Running Unity Hub from the terminal uses the current terminal configuration from ~/.profile and ~/.bashrc.
    • Running Unity Editor from the UnityHub inherits the environment setup from the Unity Hub.

docs.title: Unity installation
docs.text:
Info

V2X_E2E Simulator's Unity version is currently unity 6000.0.50f1

Follow the steps below to install Unity on your machine:

  1. Install UnityHub to manage Unity projects. Please go to Unity download page and download the DEB package link.

  2. Install Unity 6 via UnityHub.

    • Open new terminal, navigate to directory where UnityHub.AppImage is download and execute the following command (or find the unityhub icon and run it): 
      ./UnityHub.AppImage
    • Make sure you have the V2X repository cloned and ROS 2 is not sourced. 
      git clone https://github.com/tlab-wide/V2X_E2E_Simulator.git
    • Now we add the project to unity hub
    • In this step, you have to select either 'V2X_E2E_Simulator'.

    Warning

    You may see a window during this step that says you need to install the Editor first. The window provides two options: Open and Cancel. At this stage, the Open button does not function, so select Cancel to continue instructions.

    Warning

    If you see this message select the Yes, for these and other files that might be found later

    • Then, you will see this error (if you don't already have the exact version of Unity 6).
    • To fix this issue, install the correct version by clicking on the warning sign and selecting the shown version.
    • Only select the Linux Build Support. If you add other packages, you won't face any problems, but the installation will take longer. You can also install other packages later.
    • After successful installation the version will be available under the Installs tab in Unity Hub (your Unity6 can be different in minor version section).

Warning

If you get the safe mode dialog when starting UnityEditor, you may need to install openssl.

  1. Download libssl $ wget http://security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/o/openssl1.0/libssl1.0.0_1.0.2n-1ubuntu5.13_amd64.deb
  2. Install sudo dpkg -i libssl1.0.0_1.0.2n-1ubuntu5.13_amd64.deb

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
The repository comes as a workspace by itself. To build the workspace follow the steps below:

  • Clone this repository to some desired folder: 

    git clone git@github.com:hoosh-ir/autoware.git

  • Navigate to the root of the workspace: 

    cd autoware

  • Execute the ansible script to download and install system dependencies: 

    ./setup-dev-env.sh

  • Install ROS dependencies: 

    source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
rosdep install -y --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro $ROS_DISTRO

  • Build the workspace: 

    colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

docs.title: Memory Issues At Build Time
docs.text:
Building Autoware requires and enormous amount RAM (about 32GB). If you have insufficient memory, use the following commands to allocate 32GB of swap file: 

# Optional: Check the current swapfile
free -h

# Remove the current swapfile
sudo swapoff /swapfile
sudo rm /swapfile

# Create a new swapfile
sudo fallocate -l 32G /swapfile
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile

# Optional: Check if the change is reflected
free -h

docs.title: Loading PCD Files in Unity
docs.text: Loading Point Cloud Data (PCD) files into Unity can be challenging and often requires a paid solution. In this project, we've utilized the Pcx repository available on GitHub. However, it's important to note that Pcx is primarily designed to work with .ply files. We recommend using CloudCompare to convert .pcd files to .ply. In the initial step, simply open the .pcd file and make sure not to change anything related to the position of the points.

docs.title: Conversion Process in CloudCompare
docs.text:
The first challenge of importing a PCD file into Unity is correcting the dimensions. You must apply the following transformation in the opening window when you import your file in CloudCompare.

Note : Sometimes, you may not find a similar opening. In this case, first save your model as a PLY file using CloudCompare, then load the PLY file again and continue with the steps below.

When loading a PCD file into CloudCompare, pay close attention to the XYZ transformations, as illustrated below:

Ensure that you accurately fill out the input fields based on your data:

After configuring the transformations, save the file in the .ply binary format.

docs.title: Integrating .PLY Files into Unity
docs.text:
To use the converted .ply files in Unity, you will first need to install PCX. Begin by locating the manifest.json file in the Unity project’s Packages folder.

Note : After importing the model into Unity, you need to set the X scale to -1, so the model aligns exactly in the correct position.

Once PCX is installed, you can drag and drop the .ply files into your Unity environment. However, for optimal performance, it is advisable to clean up previously added project files. This practice ensures a smoother engine performance and enhances the quality and placement of 3D models prior to conducting simulation tests.

docs.title: Point Cloud with Color
docs.text: You can preserve or generate colors for your point cloud before exporting to .ply by using CloudCompare. PCX will read vertex colors automatically from the .ply, so there’s no need to assign a material in Unity for basic color display.

docs.title: 1) Start from your PCD (or PLY) in CloudCompare
docs.text:
• Open the file and apply the same XYZ transform rules described earlier (don’t re-center unless your pipeline requires it).
  • Verify in the Properties panel whether the cloud already has Colors (RGB) and/or Scalar Fields (e.g., intensity, elevation).

docs.title: 2) If your data already contains RGB
docs.text:
• Confirm that Colors are present and look correct in the 3D view.
  • (Optional) Improve legibility:
  • Edit → Colors → Enhance RGB (contrast/brightness)
  • Edit → Colors → Saturate colors (avoid over-saturation)
  • Keep coordinates unchanged to avoid extra flips later in Unity.

docs.title: 3) If Your Data Has No RGB — Generate Colors from a Scalar Field
docs.text: If your point cloud lacks native RGB values, you can colorize it using scalar fields such as intensity, elevation (Z), classification, or distance. CloudCompare provides several built-in methods to visualize and export these as actual colors in your .ply.

docs.title: 🟩 Option A — Color by Height (Z-axis)
docs.text:
This is the fastest and most intuitive method for topographic or structural data.

  1. Select your cloud in the DB tree.
  2. Go to Edit → Colors → Height Ramp.
  3. In the pop-up, adjust the Min/Max height range to fit your dataset.
  4. Choose a color ramp (e.g., “Blue to Red”, “Jet”, or “Rainbow”).
  5. Confirm and view the gradient applied from low to high elevation.

Tip: This is great for terrain, buildings, and scans where height variation is meaningful.

docs.title: 🟨 Option B — Color by Intensity or Any Scalar Field
docs.text:
For LiDAR or scanner data, intensity or reflectance fields can give visual cues about surface materials.

  1. Ensure your cloud contains a scalar field (e.g., Intensity).
  2. You can verify this in the Properties panel — look for a drop-down labeled Scalar field.
  3. Set it active via: Edit → Scalar fields → Set as active (or use the SF toolbar menu).
  4. Visualize the range with the Color Scale bar on the right:
  5. Adjust Min/Max values to avoid washed-out or oversaturated regions.
  6. Experiment with linear, logarithmic, or custom gradients.
  7. Once satisfied, convert it to real RGB colors:
  8. Edit → Colors → Convert SF to RGB.
  9. (Optional) Fine-tune colors again and repeat the conversion if you modify the scale.

🎥 Video Reference If you’d like a step-by-step demonstration of this process, watch the video below. It shows how to apply color ramps, adjust scalar ranges, and export the result as a colored .ply file.

docs.title: 🟦 Option C — Color by Classification or Segments
docs.text:
When working with classified LiDAR data or segmented point clouds (e.g., ground, vegetation, buildings), assign unique colors per class.

  1. If a classification field exists, make it active: Edit → Scalar fields → Set as active → choose Classification.
  2. Apply a color scheme:
  3. Edit → Colors → Convert SF to RGB — for class-based palettes, or
  4. Edit → Colors → Set Unique Colors — to manually differentiate objects.
  5. Verify that each class or segment now displays a distinct, consistent color.

Use case: Useful for visually inspecting segmented datasets before Unity import.

After applying any of the above methods, confirm the point cloud displays the expected colors in CloudCompare’s 3D view. You can then proceed to export it as a Binary PLY with the “Save colors” option enabled to preserve your colorization.

Tip: If the colors look washed out, narrow the scalar field’s min/max range so the gradient spans the actual data.

docs.title: 4) Optional: Compute normals (for nicer point visuals)
docs.text:
• Edit → Normals → Compute
  • Use KNN with a neighbor count that matches your point density (e.g., 16–32 for dense scans, 8–16 for sparse).
  • Normals are not required for color, but can help with round/disk rendering styles.

docs.title: 5) Export with colors to Binary PLY
docs.text: • File → Save → pick PLY and choose Binary (smaller, faster to load).

docs.title: Kashiwa Scene Names
docs.text: The signalised intersections of the Kashiwa scene (Enviroment copy/intersectionsFixed/ in the environment prefab) and their traffic lights are named after the CooL4 DM signal sheet and the Lanelet2 map. The names are plain ASCII (romaji), so they are safe in logs, configs and code.

docs.title: Intersections
docs.text:
The five bus-route intersections use their DM names. The others are named after the nearest OpenStreetMap landmark (OSM names only 東大前 itself).

docs.title: Approach IDs (方路)
docs.text: For the five DM intersections they are the IDs of the DM signal sheet. For the others they are numbered clockwise, starting with the leg closest to north (1 = that leg, 2 = the next leg clockwise, …).

docs.title: Traffic lights
docs.text:
Each light carries the CooL4 signal IDs it shows (spec §3.6.3: vehicle ID = inbound 方路 × 0x10 + outbound 方路, pedestrian ID = crossed 方路 × 0x10):

<Intersection>_V_0x<k>1-0x<k><N>_<i>    vehicle head for traffic entering from 方路 k (N = number of approaches)
<Intersection>_P_0x<k>0_<i>             pedestrian head of the crosswalk across 方路 k

<i> numbers the heads of the same approach (1, 2, …, clockwise around the centre). Examples: Kakeiken_V_0x21-0x23_1 is the first vehicle head for traffic entering 科警研 from 方路2 (signal IDs 0x21–0x23). Wakashiba_P_0x40_2 is the second pedestrian head of the crosswalk across 若柴 方路4.

docs.title: RSUs
docs.text: The RSUs follow the route: Ganken (RSU ID 0x12020001), Kakeiken_A and Kakeiken_B (0x12020002, 0x12020003), Midblock (0x12020004, between 科警研 and 若柴) and Wakashiba (0x12020005). Sensor IDs are unique within each RSU. From v3.2 they are defined in config/scenarios/<name>/rsus.yaml (see RSUs and Pseudo Sensors); in the v3.1 scenes they are the groups under RSUs/Pseudo Sensors setup (RSU1_Ganken_CooL4, RSU2_Kakeiken_CooL4, RSU3_Midblock, RSU4_Wakashiba). All IDs are listed in Reading the Messages.

docs.title: Where the names are used
docs.text:
Keep these in sync when you rename an intersection or a light:

  • DMSignalInfoPublisher → Traffic Intersection Name of each intersection
  • config/scenarios/<name>/rsus.yaml → traffic_signal_publishers[].intersections
  • config/scenarios/<name>/pedestrians.yaml → waypoints[].traffic_light; in the v3.1 scenes the pedestrian path configs (Assets/Configs/pedestrian_spawn*.json) and WaypointSystem waypoints → trafficLightId
  • web viewer tools/web-viewer/config/traffic_lights.yaml → unity_intersection

docs.title: Web Viewer
docs.text:
The web viewer is a local web page that answers two questions while the simulator runs:

  1. Which topics are live? Every topic the simulator publishes is listed with its status, rate and last-message age.
  2. What do they say? Everything except raw sensor data is drawn on the Kashiwa Lanelet2 map: DM object info, DM signal info with remaining time, V2X and Autoware traffic signals, Autoware objects and the ego vehicle.

It lives in tools/web-viewer/ and runs on the simulator machine only.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
cd V2X_E2E_Simulator
tools/web-viewer/run.sh

Then open http://localhost:8080. Start the simulator before or after; the viewer picks up topics as they appear.

run.sh does the setup:

  • sources ROS 2 Humble and the v2x_e2e_msgs workspace, which it expects at ../v2x_e2e_msgs/install next to the simulator folder. Override this with MSGS_SETUP=/path/to/install/setup.bash.
  • uses the simulator's middleware settings: RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp and ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1.
  • on the first run, creates tools/web-viewer/.venv with aiohttp, leaving the system Python untouched.

Options: --port 9000 changes the port. The server binds to 127.0.0.1, so the page cannot be opened from another computer.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Simulator ──ROS 2──► server/main.py  (one Python process, rclpy + aiohttp)
                       ├─ monitor.py   discovers topics every second, subscribes to each non-raw topic,
                       │               measures rate / last-message age, keeps the latest message
                       ├─ decoders.py  turns the latest messages into map features (≤ 10 Hz),
                       │               only for the topics ticked in the page
                       └─ WebSocket /ws ──► browser: topic list (1 Hz) + map layers (≤ 10 Hz)

No Foxglove, rosbridge or other ROS packages are needed. The server subscribes with best effort QoS, which matches both reliable and best-effort publishers. Raw sensor types (PointCloud2, Image, CameraInfo, LaserScan, Imu, NavSatFix, …) are listed but never subscribed to.

docs.title: Problems
docs.text:
Every topic with an issue is listed at the top of the sidebar, grouped by reason. Each group has a short explanation, and each topic its details. Click a topic to open it in the inspector.

Group Meaning What to check 🔴 Message type missing The type is not in the sourced message workspace, so the topic cannot be received or decoded (e.g. /OBU/Sensing, Autoware DetectedObjects). Rebuild v2x_e2e_msgs with that type, or set MSGS_SETUP to a workspace that has it. 🔵 Publisher but no data A publisher exists but nothing has arrived. The publisher may be idle, or its QoS is incompatible. 🟠 Stopped publishing Messages arrived before but stopped (shows how long ago). The simulator is paused, or the publisher stopped. ⚫ Offline (no publisher) The publisher is gone. Folded by default. The simulator is stopped, or the publisher is disabled in the scene.

When every topic is offline, the panel shows a single "Simulator not publishing" notice instead of the long list.

docs.title: Topic tree
docs.text:
Below the problems, topics are grouped by category: DM signal info, DM object info, traffic signals, Autoware objects, ego vehicle, control, clock and other. Within each category they form a tree that follows the topic names, for example v2x › object_info › DSRC. Namespaces with a single child are merged (awsim/ground_truth).

  • Branches show how many of their topics are live (3/20) and badges for problems inside them (1 no data, 2 type missing). Their checkbox ticks or unticks every drawable topic below them; it is part-filled when only some are ticked.
  • Topics show their status dot, rate or problem, and colour swatch. A topic with delayed copies (/DSRC, /Cellular) has a ▸ to show them.
  • Branches with more than six topics, and every topic's delayed copies, start folded. Typing in the filter box expands everything that matches. The folding and tick choices are remembered in the browser.
Status dot Meaning 🟢 live Messages are arriving; the rate is measured over the last 3 s. 🟠 stale Messages arrived before but have stopped (the age is shown). 🔵 no data yet A publisher exists but nothing has been received. ⚫ offline No publisher any more (e.g. the simulator was stopped). 🔴 type missing The message type is not in the sourced workspace, so the topic cannot be decoded. half green (branches) some, but not all, topics below are live

Tick a topic to draw it on the map. Click its name to see its type, publishers, rate, message count, bandwidth and a summary of the last message. Delayed copies (…/DSRC, …/Cellular) start unticked, because they duplicate other topics.

docs.title: Map layers
docs.text:
Data Topic types How it is placed Lanelet2 map maps/lanelet2.geojson Lanes, lane borders, crosswalks, stop lines and traffic-light positions DM object info dm_object_info_msgs/ObjectInfoArray Latitude/longitude and heading from the message, drawn as boxes of the reported size Signal heads dm_signal_info_msgs/SignalInfoArray, v2x_msgs/V2XSignals, Autoware TrafficSignalArray / TrafficLightGroupArray At the real signal positions of config/traffic_lights.yaml (see Signal heads) Other traffic lights V2X / Autoware traffic signals whose ID is not in the config A dot at the Lanelet2 traffic light with that regulatory-element or way ID RSU sensors rsus.yaml of the default scenario + health of their object-info topics Sensor icon and field-of-view sector (see Sensors) Autoware objects PredictedObjects, DetectedObjects, TrackedObjects Map frame (map, obj) converted to lat/lon. Ego-relative frames such as bus are placed with the ego pose. Ego vehicle /awsim/ground_truth/vehicle/pose and other PoseStamped / Odometry topics in the map frame Cyan box

Each topic has its own colour (the swatch in the list). Layers of topics that are not live are dimmed. Click any object or signal to open the inspector. It shows the decoded fields: for example the object ID split into RSU / sensor / object number, the CooL4 light colour and the full remaining-time schedule.

The overlay toggles under the legend switch the signal heads, the sensors, the sensor coverage sectors and the disabled sensors on and off. Overlapping heads and sensors (several on one pole) are stacked automatically.

Background map (online) overlays GSI tiles when the machine has internet. Everything else, including the Lanelet2 map, works offline.

docs.title: Signal heads
docs.text:
Every vehicle and pedestrian signal head of the five bus-route intersections is drawn where it stands. Positions come from config/traffic_lights.yaml.

Head Shows Vehicle Three bulbs in Japanese order (green, yellow, red, left to right), green arrows (← ↑ →) if lit, remaining seconds Pedestrian Stop (red) and walk (green) figures, remaining seconds; a flashing walk figure is 青点滅

Flashing lights blink. Zoomed out (below 17.3) the heads show bulbs only; below 15.8 they are hidden.

Where the state comes from, in order of preference:

  1. CooL4 DM signal info: the SignalInfo whose crp_id matches the intersection and whose signal_id_list contains one of the head's dm_signal_ids. Only DM carries the remaining time (min_time_to_change); "—" means the light never changes (countdown stopped).
  2. V2X / Autoware traffic signals (vehicle heads only): the signal whose ID is one of the head's lanelet_regulatory_elements or lanelet_light_ways. These messages have no remaining time, so no seconds are shown.

A head with no data is greyed out; a head fed by a topic that is not live is dimmed with a dashed border. Click a head to see both sources side by side: the DM light, remaining time and full schedule, and the V2X/Autoware elements.

docs.title: config/traffic_lights.yaml
docs.text:
A human-readable file, one block per intersection and approach (方路):

intersections:
  - name: 科警研 (Kakeiken)
    crp_id: 798721            # 0x000c3001
    unity_intersection: 'Kakeiken'
    center: {lat: 35.896047, lon: 139.94182}
    approaches:
      - id: 2                  # 方路2
        direction: south
        bearing_deg: 160        # from the centre towards this leg
        vehicle:
          dm_signal_ids: [0x21, 0x22, 0x23]
          lanelet_regulatory_elements: [166940]
          lanelet_light_ways: [166935, 166947]
          heads:
            - {lat: 35.895915, lon: 139.94194, facing_deg: 160}
            - {lat: 35.8961811, lon: 139.9417231, facing_deg: 160}
        pedestrian:                 # crosswalk across this approach
          dm_signal_ids: [0x20]
          heads:
            - {lat: 35.8959157, lon: 139.9418385, facing_deg: 160}
            - {lat: 35.8959551, lon: 139.9419562, facing_deg: 160}
  • Vehicle heads were placed on the Lanelet2 traffic_light poles of the regulatory elements whose lanes enter from that approach. These are the same regulatory elements the simulator's TrafficLightLaneletID components carry.
  • Pedestrian heads sit at the two ends of the crosswalk across the approach; the Lanelet2 map has no pedestrian lights. 東大前 方路1 has no crosswalk in the map, so it has no pedestrian head. Add one by hand if needed.
  • Editing: move a head by changing its lat/lon, add or remove heads freely. Restart the viewer to load the change.
  • Re-deriving positions: python3 tools/web-viewer/scripts/build_signal_config.py /path/to/lanelet2_map.osm fills only approaches without heads. --force recomputes all of them, overwriting hand edits.

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text:
The Live view draws the RSU pseudo sensors of the default scenario of the simulator configuration (config/scenarios/<default>/rsus.yaml, see RSUs and Pseudo Sensors). It draws exactly what the simulator builds at Play. Each sensor is drawn as an icon (C = camera, L = lidar) with its coverage sector. The icon gets a green halo when one of its object-info topics is live. Labels appear from zoom 18. Click a sensor for all its settings and the live status of its topics.

Field in the inspector Meaning type RSU_CAMERA or RSU_LIDAR (from the kind of its sensor type) enabled The RSU and the sensor are enabled. Disabled sensors are shown only with Disabled sensors ticked. group, near RSU name and location position, heading_deg, pitch_deg Pose of the sensor (heading clockwise from north) h_fov_deg, v_fov_deg Half-angles, as MockSensor uses them (it detects |yaw| ≤ Hfov). The config gives full angles, so the drawn sector is 2 × h_fov_deg wide. range_m MockSensor.maxDistance rsu_ids, topics The RSU ID and the object-info topics that carry the sensor's objects (its own topics, the merged publishers of its RSU and their network copies)

The page reloads the list when it is opened, so sensors saved in the Settings tab appear after a page reload. tools/web-viewer/config/sensors.yaml (hand-written, v3.1) is used only when the repository has no config/ folder.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The Settings switch in the top bar opens an editor for the simulator configuration (config/ of the repository). Its tabs match the configuration files:

Tab Edits On the map Simulation Time scale, seed, ego vehicle and start pose, sun (time of day), fog, loggers Ego marker (drag; Place on map) with its heading RSUs & sensors RSUs, pseudo sensors, object-info, Autoware-object and traffic-signal publishers Drag sensors; coverage sectors; Place on map adds a sensor to the selected RSU Vehicles Traffic settings, vehicle types, spawn points, branch ratios Simulator lanes. Click a lane for its number and next lanes, then Spawn vehicles here or Set branch ratios. The selected lane is blue and branch targets are orange. Signals Step durations of every signalised intersection, with what each step shows and the cycle length — Pedestrians Paths, spawn rate, cyclist share, lights to wait for Path lines; drag the points of the selected path; Add waypoints on map Teleports Gates and their targets Trigger boxes (drag); Pick target lanes on map; random target points Raw sensors LiDARs and cameras: topics, rate, resolution, on/off World-mounted sensors (drag); Place new sensor on map Defaults Pseudo-sensor types, noise and network profiles (shared by all scenarios) —
  • Save checks all files with the same rules as the simulator. If something is wrong, it writes nothing and lists the problems. Saved files keep their comments.
  • Discard reloads the saved files. Reset to default restores the files of the current tab from config/factory/.
  • New… copies the current scenario under a new name. Make default writes config/default_scenario.txt.
  • Changes apply the next time the simulation starts.
  • Press Esc to stop a map tool.

The lanes come from config/maps/traffic_lanes.json. In Unity, V2X → Config → Export Traffic Lanes For The Web Viewer writes it. The simulator's lane numbers are not the Lanelet2 IDs of the map file, so pick lanes on these lines, not on the grey Lanelet2 lanes.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text: Source Conversion DM messages Already WGS84 (1e-7 deg) Autoware / AWSIM map frame Local coordinates of MGRS square 54SVE: UTM(EPSG:32654) = map_xy + (400000, 3900000). build_map.py derives this offset from the Lanelet2 local_x/local_y tags (residual 0 m). Ego-relative frames Rotated and translated with the latest ego pose

docs.title: Using another map or intersections
docs.text:
• Map: python3 tools/web-viewer/scripts/build_map.py /path/to/lanelet2_map.osm (the Kashiwa map is in simulator_maps_v3.1.1.zip, see Download) regenerates maps/lanelet2.geojson and maps/lanelet2_meta.json.
  • Signal heads: edit config/traffic_lights.yaml (see Signal heads). The CRP and signal IDs match the Signal Info mapping.
  • Sensors: edit them in the Settings tab or in config/scenarios/<name>/rsus.yaml.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check "No topics yet" Is the simulator running? Are ROS_DOMAIN_ID and ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY the same in both terminals? A topic shows type missing The type is not in the sourced v2x_e2e_msgs build. Rebuild the workspace, or point MSGS_SETUP to one that has it. Autoware objects in a relative frame are not drawn The ego pose topic /awsim/ground_truth/vehicle/pose must be live; the topic summary says so. Port already in use run.sh --port 9000

docs.title: Engine Crashes Repeatedly on Startup
docs.text:
If the V2X simulator crashes repeatedly during launch, try clearing temporary and cached data:

  1. Fully close the application (and Unity Editor, if applicable).
  2. Navigate to your simulator’s root directory (or Unity project folder if running from source).
  3. Delete the following folders (if they exist):
  4. Logs/ (in your first try only remove the logs)
  5. Library/
  6. Temp/
  7. Relaunch the simulator.

Note: Unity regenerates these folders automatically on startup. Removing them forces a clean reimport of assets and clears corrupted cache files, which often resolves persistent crashes or startup failures.

docs.title: Stop Lines Don't Work with Traffic Lines
docs.text:
• StopLine Reference Not Assigned The TrafficLane component requires a StopLine reference, and the referenced StopLine GameObject must have a TrafficLight component. If either condition is not met, the code will skip processing the lane entirely.

  • Waypoint Positioning The first waypoint of your approach lane must be positioned at or before the physical stop line. If the waypoint is placed after the stop line, vehicles will cross the stop line before stopping.

  • Lane Connectivity (most important reason) The approach lane must include the intersection lane in its "Next Lanes" array. Without this connection, vehicles cannot "look ahead" to detect the traffic light state.
